Peter,

**The SAVE America Act has the Establishment in full-blown panic mode.**

_And I love it._

Because every time the D.C. cartel starts clutching their pearls, you know we’re directly over the target.

This bill isn’t controversial. It’s not divisive.

**It’s a wrecking ball aimed straight at the corrupt political machine that has been looting this country for decades.**

---

_The same Republicans who campaign on “America First” and then fold like cheap lawn chairs. The same Democrats who think borders are racist and inflation is imaginary. The same permanent bureaucrats who believe they’re royalty and you’re the peasant class._

**They HATE the SAVE America Act because it strips power away from them.**

_Secure elections?_ They stall.
_Secure borders?_ They stall.
_Government accountability?_ They stall.

_Why?_
Because chaos benefits the ruling class.

A weak border means cheap labor and more control. A confused election system means more manipulation. A bloated federal government means more leverage over your life.

_This isn’t incompetence. This is intentional._

**The SAVE America Act is a declaration of war on the political aristocracy in Washington.**

That’s why they smear it and anyone who supports it. Including me.

All I say to that is **GOOD.**

I’m not running for Senate to be liked by lobbyists or invited to Georgetown dinner parties.

_I’m running to confront the fraud in both parties that sold out Minnesota and America._

The Establishment wants compliance. I want confrontation.

**The SAVE America Act isn’t radical. What’s radical is letting this corrupt system keep grinding you down while pretending everything is normal.**

name: Sarah McBride
subject: Consequences

body:
ACA enrollment has dropped by over a million people.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=2817%2E21716%2E6PNRgg)
The consequences many of us feared are here.
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260212-1.ha8CDN&amount=5&%3Brefcode=em20260212-2817&t=2&akid=2817%2E21716%2E6PNRgg)
After congressional Republicans allowed the Affordable Care Act subsidies to expire at the end of last year, **over a million people have already dropped their coverage after seeing their health care premiums skyrocket.**
It didn’t have to be this way.
The majority party in Congress could’ve extended the subsidies that helped millions of working people afford insurance, but they chose to let them expire.
When I think about the consequences of these callous decisions, I think about my late husband, Andy.
Andy was diagnosed with terminal cancer. We were fortunate to have health care — and that access didn’t take away the pain or fear, but it gave us something priceless: time. Time to hope, to love, to create more memories with each other. Time that so many families never get.
I carry Andy with me in this work. I carry every family who is holding on, hoping that they won’t be the next ones to lose their health care. That’s why I can’t look at enrollment numbers or budget line items without seeing the real people behind them. The parent deciding between renewing coverage or paying the rent, or the patient spacing out treatments because the copay is too high.
**No one should face this reality. And we cannot allow our government to continue to make decisions without regard for the human cost.** This fight is urgent for millions of families across the country, and it’s personal for me.
[**Will you chip in $5 today to help me continue to fight for affordable health care and make sure no one has to go without the care they need?**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260212-1.ha8CDN&refcode=em20260212-2817&amount=5&t=3&akid=2817%2E21716%2E6PNRgg)

Thank you,
Sarah

Feb. 12, 2026**
---
**_STATE OF THE RACE:_ _Deb is officially on the ballot — but this is NOT a safe blue seat._**
---
* The party of New Mexico's governor has FLIPPED every eight years for decades.

* Races up and down the ballot in our state are getting closer and closer, with Democratic margins shrinking dramatically between 2018 and 2024.

* With FIVE Republican opponents vying for this seat, Deb is already facing right-wing attacks, and this race could see unprecedented dark money pouring into New Mexico.

---
| | **_WHO DEB IS:_** _**Deb's running a different kind of campaign.**_
---
* Unlike her opponents, Deb doesn't come from wealth, and she's not backed by billionaires — this campaign is powered by the people.

* Over the last year since launching this campaign, she has built a true grassroots movement, visiting and earning support in all 33 counties in New Mexico and holding events in every corner of the state.

* From Shiprock to Las Cruces, Deb has stood alongside workers fighting for better wages, joined picket lines, and listened to people struggling with healthcare, affordability, safety in their communities, and more.

* Deb launched her vision, a New Mexico for New Mexicans: strengthening education, lowering costs for families, expanding access to healthcare, and delivering real public safety rooted in prevention and trust. She’ll help kids read earlier, put more money back in people’s pockets, protect and expand the coverage families rely on, make New Mexico a renewable energy titan, and stand up for New Mexicans so they can raise families and build a future here at home.

* She is a tested leader who has stood up to Trump and his extremist allies before — and is ready to do it again. As governor, she will stand up to ICE overreach, defend civil rights, safeguard public spaces, and protect New Mexicans so families can live without fear.

---
She’s ready to make progress for New Mexican families and fight for a brighter future for each and every one of us. And with Donald Trump slashing benefits and tearing families apart, the stakes couldn't be higher.

**But she can’t do it alone.**
---
| | **_HOW CAN YOU HELP?_** **_This is where you come in._**
---
* A grassroots campaign like this one relies on everyday people like you chipping in what you can, when you can — **_[$5 here](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5042?refcode=jtk260-fr-nd&t=4&akid=7472%2E400544%2EPpGTKv)_** , **_[$25 there](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5123?refcode=jtk260-fr-nd&t=5&akid=7472%2E400544%2EPpGTKv)_** , that's how Deb is going to raise the resources she needs to keep New Mexico blue.

* February is always a tough month for fundraising. But the timing couldn't be worse. Now that Deb is officially on New Mexico's ballot for governor, reaching every goal is especially important. And we know this will be one of the most competitive and expensive races in the country.

* To set us up for success, we have an ambitious $15,000 daily fundraising goal to ensure Deb can fight back against her self-funding opponents' attacks, get ads on the air in critical markets, and continue traveling across the state connecting with voters.

---
**_[Can we count on your support right now to help us get there and make sure Deb has the resources she needs as we ramp up toward Election Day?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4677?refcode=jtk260-fr-nd&t=6&akid=7472%2E400544%2EPpGTKv)_**

Dylan McArthur

| Dear Fellow American,

I wasn't planning on sharing this, but it's something you need to see...
Recently, I asked one of our lead investigators to prepare an _internal report_ on the major Leftist organizations and funders behind the **growing****lawfare campaign AGAINST election integrity.**
**Please read the _confidential_ excerpt below.**
The findings reveal the organization and financing behind the **Anti-Election Integrity Movement** and underscores how much _[the support of generous patriots like you helps us fight back](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79612&L=30946&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0yMTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3Jz&hash=aafc90fdace25a5a1871d30fa9a66413e29290f69056683c8a490d5fbaf2a4d2)_.
**_INTERNAL USE ONLY_**
**_Protecting Free, Fair, and Honest Elections: What Judicial Watch Is Up Against_**

* * *

_Left-wing politicians, blue state election administrators, and leftist organizations have launched a blitzkrieg of LAWFARE to destroy our most fundamental election safeguards._
__This LAWFARE is not a grassroots phenomenon__ _._
_Rather, it is a coordinated attack by a network of well-funded nonprofits and political actors with ties to former Democrat administrations._
_The following are the_ __key people and organizations involved__ _, and their sources of financial support._
**_Democracy Docket / Free Election Fund_**
_Founded by Democrat attorney**Marc Elias** , Democracy Docket regularly litigates to block and dismantle election integrity measures. _
_Elias served as General Counsel for the presidential campaigns of Hillary Clinton and John Kerry, when he**hired Christopher Steele** 's firm to produce the now **infamous dossier** of fabrications regarding Trump and Russia._
_His groups are sponsored by the Hopewell Fund, a Democrat nonprofit funded by**George Soros** , Pierre Omidyar, Reid Hoffman, and Swiss billionaire Hansjorg Wyss._
_Since 2020, they have received**$13 million** in direct grant funding from the **Open Society Foundations,** and as of October 2025, Elias' firm was engaged in at least 63 "voting rights" lawsuits._
**_The Campaign Legal Center_**
_Founded in 2002, this group has emerged as a**central figure** in the fight **against election integrity.**_
_It**challenged** Louisiana over S.B. 436, which requires **proof of citizenship for voters** in the state, Congressional redistricting efforts, **voter list maintenance,** and has sought to restore **voting rights for felons** and **stop voter ID** requirements. _
_They have received more than $1 million from the Open Society Foundations, more than_** _$2.5 million_** _from_** _convicted fraudster Sam Bankman-Fried_** _. Other donors include the Sandler Foundation, the John D. and Catherine T._**_MacArthur Foundation_** _, and the Democracy Fund launched by the Omidyar Network._
**_American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU)_**
_The ACLU and its state affiliates have filed more than**100 lawsuits against the Trump administration** in 2025. _
__The ACLU 's Recent cases include__ _:_
_-**Challenging**_** _voter ID requirements_** _in _President Trump 's_ executive order_
_-**Asking the courts** to compel Mississippi to create _additional majority-black Congressional districts__
_-**Challenging** New Hampshire's H.B. 1569, which requires residents to provide proof of citizenship to register to vote_
_-**Seeking to force** Pennsylvania to count _mail-in ballots_ without proper dates._
_The ACLU and its affiliates are funded by the**Open Society Foundations** , including a **$15 million** grant awarded in 2022. Other major donors include the **Rockefeller** and **Ford Foundations** , the Carnegie Corporation, and former **Facebook** Chief Operating Officer Sheryl Sandberg._
**_NAACP Legal Defense Fund_**
_The NAACP and its legal defense fund have filed numerous lawsuits challenging election integrity efforts, including**redistricting** plans in **Texas and Missouri,** proof-of-citizenship requirements in **President Trump** 's executive order, and Florida's S.B. 90, which sought to protect **voting by mail** from fraud._
**_Jonathan Soros_** _, son of George Soros, serves on the Board of Directors. The_ _organization has received nearly**$16 million** from the **Open Society Foundations**_ _since 2019 and at least**$2.25 million** from the Jennifer and Jonathan _
**_Soros Foundation_** _and additional grant funding from the_** _Tides Foundation_** _._
**_Democracy Defenders_**
_Founded in 2024 by longtime Democrat activist and lawyer Norm Eisen, Democracy Defenders and its 501(c)4 affiliate Democracy Defenders Action were created for the explicit purpose of launching legal challenges to**election integrity**. _
_The organization has already received**$5 million** from the **Open Society Foundations.**_
_In June 2025, it joined a lawsuit seeking to preserve**birthright citizenship**. It has also sued to compel Pennsylvania to accept **mail-in ballots** containing errors, including those**lacking a signature**._
**_Williams J. Brennan Center for Justice_**
_This group operates from New York University 's School of Law. It has sued to **prevent** multiple states from **cleaning voter rolls** , **opposed ID****requirements** for voting by mail, and worked to restore voting rights to convicted felons._
_The Brennan Center has received grant**funding** from **Soros ' Foundation** to Promote Open Society, more than **$1 million** from a subsidiary of the Pew Charitable Trusts and the **Ford Foundation,** and $155,000 from the **Tides Foundation**._

💰 Grocery prices are too damn high.

🗳️ And many are deeply concerned about our civil rights, democracy, and basic freedoms.
These aren’t political talking points – they’re real concerns from real people. And that’s exactly why I’m running for U.S. Senate in Michigan. Because when I see a problem, I get to work:
✅ I helped save 200,000 Michigan jobs as part of President Obama’s Auto Rescue Task Force.

✅ I led the charge to bring semiconductor manufacturing back to Michigan.

✅ I introduced the No Tariffs on Groceries Act to stop reckless food tariffs that are raising grocery prices.

✅ And I filed articles of impeachment against RFK Jr. for endangering public health.
I was recently named one of the most effective lawmakers in Congress – because I pride myself on showing up, listening, and delivering for working families.

Now I’m bringing that same grit to this battleground Senate race. With polls showing I’m the Democrat best positioned to defeat MAGA Republican Mike Rogers, GOP megadonors are set to spend millions to flip this seat red.

_—Democracy Docket_ We don’t have much time. Just last night, the U.S. House of Representatives voted to pass the SAVE Act, a sweeping voter suppression bill backed by Donald Trump that could block tens of millions of Americans from voting. The bill will head to the U.S. Senate next. subject: My decision
body:
We’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. The President of the United States threatened my life, personally. I’ve got the weight of the executive branch bearing down on me right now.
---
Hey Derek, it’s Mark Kelly. Seven years ago, I was making a decision about whether I was going to run for the Senate. I knew it would be a lot of work. A lot of time away from home. A lot of time away from family. I knew it wouldn’t be easy. But after two years of Donald Trump and a Republican-held Senate doing just about everything they wanted, I knew I couldn’t sit on the sidelines. I had to do something. So, I ran. And, somehow, we won. But then we had to turn around and run all over again to win another term after that. And, thanks to your support, we won that one, too. I’m grateful every day that I get to wake up, walk out the door, and defend the American people, our democracy, and our Constitution. It’s one of the greatest honors of my life. And I’ve never forgotten that I wouldn’t be here without your help. We’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. The President of the United States threatened my life, personally. I’ve got the weight of the executive branch bearing down on me right now. After everything you’ve already done for me, I shouldn’t have to ask you for more. But that’s what I need to do. name: Carmela Conroy
subject: Cheerleading for a compromised prosecutor
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CONROY FOR CONGRESS
body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=a3eec5fc7e&e=a7b299e420)
| | | | | |
Peter,

**The Department of Justice has released millions of pages from the Epstein files** , revealing hundreds of powerful people tied to Jeffrey Epstein’s heinous child sex trafficking ring - too few have faced any accountability.

This week, when our nation’s top prosecutor Pam Bondi was questioned about the files, she defied House members who asked about redactions that appear to protect powerful people. She refused to look survivors in the eye; she literally turned her back on them.
---
[|
---](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=6da7c53dca&e=a7b299e420)
| |
Our freshman representative, Michael Baumgartner, when given the chance, didn’t demand answers for survivors. **His question:**[_**“How are you guys getting this stuff so right?”**_](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=e4c8f3ef1f&e=a7b299e420)

So right? His job isn’t to cheerlead for the Attorney General. It’s to represent us in Washington’s 5th District and advocate for accountability.

**Our representative has made it clear where he stands.** He has publicly said that White House Deputy Chief of Staff Steven Miller and AG Pam Bondi looked to him and other Republican members of the House Judiciary Committee to “back stop” them. To shield them from consequences, instead of providing the check and balance on executive abuse of authority.

When I was a Spokane County Deputy Prosecutor, I stood up for survivors of sexual assault in juvenile court. The majority of juvenile sexual offenders were themselves victims of sexual assault, and my speaking up for survivors broke the cycle of abuse. It’s not comfortable. It’s not fun. But it is essential that prosecutors speak for the most vulnerable, not to protect the powerful.

**I’m running for Congress because we deserve someone who answers to us, not to extremist party elites.**

Because in Eastern Washington, we believe in fairness. We believe in protecting kids. And we believe nobody is above the law.

[**If you’re with me, if you believe survivors deserve justice - and that no one, no matter how powerful or well connected, should be above the rule of law, please sign on now:**](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=e48db50195&e=a7b299e420)
---
| [ADD YOUR NAME](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=6d8fe867a3&e=a7b299e420)
---
| |
If Michael Baumgartner won’t stand with survivors, we must make it clear that we do.

The more we use our voices in solidarity, the harder we are to ignore.

Carmela Conroy

body:
The worst part of this new law? The Ohio legislature wrote and passed this bill without any input from the officials across the state who actually run the elections.
“ It’s a solution to a non-existent problem, ” said Warren County election official Bethe Goldenfield. “ I don’t see where this is doing anything to help voters. It’s only going to disenfranchise people .”
This is all part of a partisan push to preserve their own power. RUSH $35 or more to help us fight back against these attacks on mail-in voting and more >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=021226_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Bolts: Ohio Bans Grace Periods for Mail Ballots, Fulfilling Trump’s Wishes [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=021226_3&amount=25]
Ohio has made it harder to vote by mail, Team .
Senate Bill 293, which was recently signed into law, repeals Ohio’s practice of counting mail ballots that are postmarked prior to Election Day but that arrive up to four days after polls close. Now, any ballots delayed in the mail that arrive after Election Day won't count in Ohio.
This follows executive orders from President Trump, who is against mail-in voting despite voting that way himself , and has called for ending these so-called grace periods for mail ballots everywhere. Ohio’s new law follows his lead, threatening thousands of votes in the process.
We've said it before and we'll keep saying it: Mail-in balloting is safe and secure. It's a nonpartisan way for eligible voters to make their voices heard in our elections. And now it's harder for them to participate in elections in Ohio, whether they're a military member voting from overseas, someone who is immunocompromised, in a nursing home, or any other reason for voting by mail.
Defending vote-by-mail is a crucial part of protecting our fundamental right to vote. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to support mail-in voting across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=021226_3&amount=35]

Trump has long lied about mail-in voting. He's claimed mail-in voting contributed to his 2020 election loss, though no widespread fraud has been found. In fact, the one case of mail-in ballot fraud in Pennsylvania after the 2020 election was a man who was prosecuted for returning his dead mother's ballot for Trump .
The use of mail-in voting has become very common across the country and study after study has shown that fraud in mail-ballot voting is rare. There are also several safeguards in place nationwide to protect against fraud, including signature requirements and barcodes to track envelopes sent by officials. States have spent tens of millions of taxpayer dollars investigating voter fraud since 2020's "big lie" and found virtually nothing.
In Ohio, this new law will result in thousands of ballots being thrown out. We know this because thousands of ballots were accepted in the grace period in previous selections, some of them making the difference in local elections -- like in Warren County, where several races came down to single-digit margins.
Being blunt: There is no good-faith reason to end the vote-by-mail grace period. Just like the other Trump attacks on our elections in general and mail-in voting in particular -- this is a partisan voter suppression exercise meant to codify MAGA's power in perpetuity.

**Peter, the Department of Justice continues to carry out Trump’s crusade to undermine our democracy.** Under the repeatedly debunked claim of voter fraud, the DOJ is demanding that states turn over sensitive voter roll data — including information such as driver’s license and social security numbers — to the Department of Homeland Security.
And if states don’t comply, the DOJ is threatening to sue them. Last year alone, the DOJ sued 21 states and D.C. as part of its anti-democracy campaign. And it is continuing to do so, having just filed new lawsuits against Connecticut and Arizona.

**They’re using bald-faced lies to justify their intimidation tactics, all part of an attempt to spread distrust in our electoral process. | For those of us who believe in democratic values and live in rural areas, the choices are rarely simple. We have fewer options, wider philosophical gaps, and we are often voting for a first time candidate. Too often, the underdog.
Even for deep blue, capital D Democrats, the decision is not always straightforward. Voting in rural districts means balancing principle and strategy. But the beauty of voting is this: it is yours alone, and the only wasted vote is the one not cast.
That brings me to Congressional District 3 and [Marie Gluesenkamp Perez](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ABEsd6LX5eBNP-i2TAIgqpC3wBV9of-ndrrvnaY9P2LouYiybLJCHjIZdFx8QIHw5dnvL-bv7WQm0aSaDozO6Hi-C3K-0TzChJ7cQweqsABo1AeY26KPyZIBqRQZavfRI-xGkpEOzOlLhXZo7E6s0utgeC1uRgm4fErK8P0FOHs=&c=NzVGgPUzTPEBL4k9NR6oeSCN9ywuZMWNiG_1EVt1XutZOXROH7n3pg==&ch=y5-sMeFeIn22X6kiv3taHdNfs4HqyXWdj9vQ7szTjHVV-ssrRkdTwA==), a [Blue Dog Democrat](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ABEsd6LX5eBNP-i2TAIgqpC3wBV9of-ndrrvnaY9P2LouYiybLJCHjIZdFx8QIHwDAmMI9Wf8m5_x5gMvaUQmNODrbljokEfO_OegGrGdbpHLrX0c3dwXi8BI9thKotOTJMfnHHfcrocqnBOs_BNiQ==&c=NzVGgPUzTPEBL4k9NR6oeSCN9ywuZMWNiG_1EVt1XutZOXROH7n3pg==&ch=y5-sMeFeIn22X6kiv3taHdNfs4HqyXWdj9vQ7szTjHVV-ssrRkdTwA==). She has been under scrutiny for her voting record. She reportedly votes with Republicans about 48 percent of the time, which unsettles many left leaning constituents.
The flashpoint has been her support for funding ICE. Her explanation was that fully funding ICE allows oversight and control. Reading it, I could not help but picture a tantrum throwing child being appeased in hopes of maintaining order. Who is controlling whom? Still, someone I respect reminded me that she has held this seat for two cycles. That matters. Incumbency carries weight. She knows her district.

| Facebook post February 3, 2026
But there are others in the race. [Brent Hennrich](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ABEsd6LX5eBNP-i2TAIgqpC3wBV9of-ndrrvnaY9P2LouYiybLJCHjIZdFx8QIHwPk4cm4XxV0RBVaWLElt1dxrza7XUCqnQrh3Jl_Fht-5I0a7QmjQ3XA0kWdlYmTPf7ThCXMqLI1h9cYNvH_6PJtOgybQn_Qce&c=NzVGgPUzTPEBL4k9NR6oeSCN9ywuZMWNiG_1EVt1XutZOXROH7n3pg==&ch=y5-sMeFeIn22X6kiv3taHdNfs4HqyXWdj9vQ7szTjHVV-ssrRkdTwA==) ran in 2022 and stepped aside to consolidate votes behind her. He is now back. After her January 22 vote on ICE funding, his campaign raised 50,000 dollars in small dollar donations in ten days. Polling commissioned by his campaign suggests that only about 24 percent of her previous voters feel confident supporting her again. Many supported her more as a vote against Joe Kent than as an endorsement of her.
So what does a Democrat do? Support the incumbent because she may have the strongest path to reelection? Support a challenger whose platform aligns more closely with traditional Democratic views? Or stay home and risk handing the seat to the favored Republican, [John Braun](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ABEsd6LX5eBNP-i2TAIgqpC3wBV9of-ndrrvnaY9P2LouYiybLJCHjIZdFx8QIHwpXtGcH4MUo0OXvJcCUfTONeKbg3Wgk8E5dB68yxvYtjpXZ5TZOhptvlIUkRYfsGeT42Z044To5hPcFHA3sVS7fC2ej93WztVetFp5e9gdlg=&c=NzVGgPUzTPEBL4k9NR6oeSCN9ywuZMWNiG_1EVt1XutZOXROH7n3pg==&ch=y5-sMeFeIn22X6kiv3taHdNfs4HqyXWdj9vQ7szTjHVV-ssrRkdTwA==)?
In Congressional District 4, I have heard Democrats say they voted for Dan Newhouse to reward his impeachment vote. Others did so out of fear that Jerrod Sessler would win. Rural Democrats make complicated choices.
But one truth remains. If Democrats show up and vote, we win. Especially in midterms, when turnout is low and margins are thin.
So vote.

Rural and Eastern counties make up some of the highest-turnout (San Juan, Garfield, Wahkiakum) and lowest-turnout (Adams, Grant, Franklin). These results follow demographics (age, ethnicity, and education level) but also reflect longstanding local nuances. When it comes to turnout, politics are often local.

I recently had an enlightening conversation with Danielle Surkatty of the [Yakima Immigration Response Network](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ABEsd6LX5eBNP-i2TAIgqpC3wBV9of-ndrrvnaY9P2LouYiybLJCHjIZdFx8QIHwyLvFxoKwtaXowinec9GONOLlmjSXBemQ5XoIdykBjWhyKYrD4uLQVITB2hFzgdbTQDG8-u1qNuigXCxR3CbZqa533yRS4zmMKU7ZFQLsfimQLrRx0hCYPvWbzv8ORPeF&c=NzVGgPUzTPEBL4k9NR6oeSCN9ywuZMWNiG_1EVt1XutZOXROH7n3pg==&ch=y5-sMeFeIn22X6kiv3taHdNfs4HqyXWdj9vQ7szTjHVV-ssrRkdTwA==), YIRN. She founded the organization in 2017, and it has grown into one of the most trusted community support networks in Central Washington.
Since the start of the Trump administration, the need for YIRN's services has grown dramatically. Yakima County now has the highest number of ICE arrests in Washington State, according to the [University of Washington Center for Human Rights.](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ABEsd6LX5eBNP-i2TAIgqpC3wBV9of-ndrrvnaY9P2LouYiybLJCHjIZdFx8QIHwMwcpsy9sq_VhEJEGcctPJPZWAGlapofJsQ0VJ0CM08yUbqtHdLlNNJtbeJaWoP35Lk2GElPgVHJzwQUD7TWWURsP7cITFTq76X2Q5aAYCfYlQA-vGdcpfg==&c=NzVGgPUzTPEBL4k9NR6oeSCN9ywuZMWNiG_1EVt1XutZOXROH7n3pg==&ch=y5-sMeFeIn22X6kiv3taHdNfs4HqyXWdj9vQ7szTjHVV-ssrRkdTwA==)
An ICE arrest is not just a statistic. It is a family crisis. Imagine living paycheck to paycheck and a spouse suddenly disappears. No clear answers. No immediate information. Just fear, uncertainty, and children who still need to be fed and protected. YIRN steps into that chaos. They accompany people to court dates. They place funds into commissary accounts. They provide gas cards and emergency support. They help secure passports for U.S. born children. They counter misinformation and ensure families understand their rights. Volunteer and ICE victim Jamie Ortiz has started a [Facebook page](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ABEsd6LX5eBNP-i2TAIgqpC3wBV9of-ndrrvnaY9P2LouYiybLJCHjIZdFx8QIHw10u-s_uWKvLPqulASqRC_Xk_QHjkTXLLLF1Xc8iGTngW0PI264X8inJUA1GsA37qpMdKkZwss7dSg1zjnv0s_Hgix4s5ubZQhxUp4moKyfapnNEIrHOqXg==&c=NzVGgPUzTPEBL4k9NR6oeSCN9ywuZMWNiG_1EVt1XutZOXROH7n3pg==&ch=y5-sMeFeIn22X6kiv3taHdNfs4HqyXWdj9vQ7szTjHVV-ssrRkdTwA==) to monitor ICE activity. It now has over twenty eight thousand followers.

Still, families remain vulnerable, and the need is real.
YIRN has built a strong coalition to support impacted families, and they rely on volunteers and direct financial contributions to sustain this work.

Showing up when someone else's world falls apart. If you cannot attend, make a contribution. If you cannot give, share the event. Silence helps no one.

## Minnesota ICE Surge Ending
Border czar Tom Homan announced Thursday that the federal immigration crackdown in Minneapolis was winding down, saying he proposed the drawdown of most of the 2,000 remaining ICE officers, and [President Trump concurred](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2upDAQhE8DmZFpwxgCB5uQvU03RD12A73yDzKeZ83tV6zmBi_7VCWVqurP1_qF7DnuvzGQKVtaI9XLUymUV7ZUuRwuY0Wf_DucbK9Kzq0g4SEkiF6tDtm_16F1ZiMCUi2ZXms5T1Jr3R5mGy3hpBWgRQV2HrXTT6VHN2qSSKplc6dJ6FXfy0c_doSDdCDnTU4Onjg3gyTHJeXub-JYDtr8O31T7mwKrTdHKefVqF8NLA0stdYuPu294vYbWG5sYHld4kMlv8Ip0AWOfJWMhVMURwoYBVsS6aSPFqjkJK5X3klQdBx3kW1EGCcNss3GnZW95-uhm0HuAdn_r1R-9OO3gX8BAAD___ZGiiA). The operation, which began late last year with more than 3,000 federal agents surging into the city, yielded over 4,000 arrests, according to the Department of Homeland Security. Homan said the decision followed an ongoing drop in confrontations with protesters and the [volume of arrests](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDvOpDAQhE9jMiO7YXgEDjYhm003RA1uD73yA2FrrLn9L-YKf_pVqUpV_57rE9lzfP3FQKa4tEaq2VMpdK28U-Vy2Asr-uQ_4eQ9V7J2BQWDVCB1t1pk_1n7xhpHBNQ1ZPQ4qnlS4zg2h6FHT9qNk570rrfOwkydw033AyAqPTVs7jQFutNaDfrREvbKgpqdmixsOItekeWSrvZ_4lgOcv6T3nS1ewqNN0cpZxbdHwGLgKXW2u5bvlfcuoAlcIyUU0EBy40FLCUFeaSAUd5A7ik6uijuJL9mPJPnLB1tUoOApbmMPSt7z3kYRa9eAdl_28uvLnsb-AkAAP__LdOBig) already made. _"I don't want to see any more bloodshed,"_ he said.
## Olympics Disqualify Ukrainian over Helmet
Ukrainian skeleton racer Vladyslav Heraskevych was disqualified from the Winter Olympics on Thursday, just 45 minutes before his race, after refusing to remove a helmet honoring [more than 20 athletes and coaches](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhDAQhJ8GOk7rtYNx4SLNdZc2JdrD62Nz5kfGOcTbR0TKE6QcjTSa7_u89TeSJPPjgyb2JS79zPuWuBTOvQy8SxlDpp3Sko5plWHbOYQeAdsGsFG6DyTp6E0dfGRG1jV7ZS24Dqy19egJlXOgretadAFdq1sbaLBaoQOlbC3-XANUWilo1duFyUBAcBG6gHdylQEOUpZ8-VpkLiPHdCwvzpdhmerkx1LWrdLvFV4rvNJ6ApzVGXKRIXGF15EzbU9-HcPYjJwmLs33M5PM3PyBNduTE5dlblzUYFjF2GkTAt21pojRMICOYKirsw_rLinJ1trKwGMiSb9vyr8Uvjz-BAAA__-rYYTb) killed in his country's war with Russia. The International Olympic Committee ruled the "helmet of remembrance" violated its ban on political statements during competition and offered compromises, including a black armband, but the medal contender refused. He argued the rule was applied inconsistently, saying other athletes displayed personal tributes at these Games [without penalty](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDuO3DAQRE9DZRTIllafgIETZevUodDDbq3aS31MckTo9sYYmBM4LlSh3vv1OX-iBNm_fuLGLi_HvHNJgXPmOIvnInmliAXDEe7tFJ8KE81goNMGtG1mQgn33FbkFmbgpmJn-96Mg-n7vlqdpXG0ntB2fmgseoKx7R-esSFg23SVuNeaAdtYazr7UTO2hsCMixkIHjiq1jBJPmL9-5A9r7yE-7g41v7YquDWnM-kmh8KJgVTKaXeH_5F8coVTOk8Yk4KpjeBgun5HVF21ldAulPAS68cMX3zdftVk6Q_TwyyCJMusmeO-l3WK4eNsy4YdfQ7wsfQjV0VHZ1FQpDU9ao1XxtK-Pcv_5fUy8HfAAAA__-zQ4_e). Some things "are more important than medals," he told reporters. President Zelenskyy said the Olympic movement "should help stop wars, not play into the hands of aggressors." Ukrainian service members have since launched a [social media campaign](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1urDAQQOGnMd2u7LEXm8LFbZCuok2bEhnPsExkfgSTJbx9tHmFtKf4ivNx7-6JC8-P9zRRlGHpZjr2QiK0dZzpYBlxS0cqSzmnlfN-EGIHGuqLhouxHSYuZ-cqjAMRkK0oGu91E7T3vhpjyHDrQ9-D65tsKafBeRyCseBzX9tUcXxpGow1RtfmdqXkNIJuBh0Q-tQopwlZlu36ufAsIw3lXJ60XfMyVSWOIuuu7D8FrYL2-1UVtG8nP__PSCvNSLMoaHdJ8rUraEGDCbdgnYXaW3DG-WqLuB5cCu-1V04_psTl15c_TXlG-AkAAP__tb50BQ) in support of the racer.
## FTC Warns Apple Over News Bias
Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson [sent a letter Wednesday to Apple CEO](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1urDAQhZ_GdKDx4IuhcHEbuk2bEvlnvExiMAJrrX37iLxCmtMc6Ts63-djeVhOvD8_7EamxLzsVK9EpdC5sKfKZQ2nrTbl9N4O9lelEBYEHFrAVvZLsJzei2qCiURIfUNGag3TCFrrZjXTRAGlU26EEKNWvRsGqyblkJzUo2vY3DRA2UsJg_zXkVUQEKYIY0BnJ6GAApd8dl-Z97JSTO_8orPzeWuSWUs5LtH_FzgLnGutnd-dv0uB840WOAMKnOUdsfi28Nb6nL9bexyJ2vtx62m_8nmtfHRr2VJzmnBUTomvQQsFz81y-h0sf7L0MvgTAAD__5ReewM) Tim Cook, warning that the company's popular News app may be violating consumer protection laws by systematically suppressing conservative news outlets. The letter followed a study by the Media Research Center, which analyzed 620 stories featured on Apple News in January and found that [none came from right-leaning outlets](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ_GdI7MGuI_BcU17v5rr0QOXoc9GRt5N0G8_Yl7hb-d0XyamT_f83egTOX1O2w4SapzwYMzimCbacGDZI0tHCHXfG47LXxgjDMYuGsDurdzDJTPeejilBABbYdT75x5fBnnXLdOz3uAZE1Izo5jwsUOD7csJln3tHYcbUfTRTPQ27439368YRhMBPNI5ivCMzzUYDCS1Hb7W6nIiimf9YPtttSty9MqsrOyvxR4Bb6ce2W5LAX-AivwBhT43ijwzzdTQWYFPux7Rn2t1XurWxVknTGJzhgKlZfeMFLQ9S0ZhXVgTaJ5fQtfml5qYWyfIPRBzXSlsQg1zKdmecdTge_aFPeDcia-OzWY1xYo_28tP7r6M8G_AAAA___foZVq). Of the total, 440 were from left-leaning sources and 180 from centrist ones, with zero articles from the _New York Post_ or _Fox News_. President Trump shared the [findings on Truth Social](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O4yAUxfGngS7R5ctAQbHSyl22WmlKi_G9jhlhYwGJlbcfZV5h2nOkX_H_uE23mHLa7__iRqEvZdrpbJl6pzqlmc7UV6zxjLnk13akuZ2EOEmQwwXkRagJY8qvSXMMC5EkxSkIa8E7sNbyNQDMaBbQCNrGCN4hoiPnvQLtSA08hbcGUighYBDmSlEDSvALOJSf0TMNhKmXev0qae8rLflVnlSvc9l4DmvvR2PqD5Mjk2Ovj762MqeY3_971FAp5r9ljxn_18d2MDkepfXG5CjEAAaM8WCM8VY5xWvA40w5pzZYpuG-xfRD8f6rPs8gvwMAAP__XO13eA). Ferguson urged Cook to conduct a "comprehensive review" and take corrective action if the app's curation does not match its terms of service, though he acknowledged the FTC cannot require Apple to promote any particular viewpoint. Apple said its app "provides access to news spanning a wide range of topics from more than 3,000 publications" and that users can tailor the feed to their interests.

Here's an unpopular opinion I didn't say out loud when I was running for office, but I'll say it now.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcfbea93-26b4-4cc1-b07e-f5982b8ea0dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### Members of Congress do not get paid enough.
Yes, I know the number. The base salary for most Members is $174,000 a year. And yes, compared to the median American household, that is a serious salary. I'm not pretending otherwise. But once you step back and look at what we claim we want out of Congress, who we claim we want to recruit, and what incentives we've built into the job, the current pay structure helps produce the exact problems everyone complains about.
This is not a sympathy post for politicians.
**This is a post about incentives.**
#### The Competition Problem
If we genuinely want Congress to include more ambitious, capable, working-age professionals, the current salary often functions like a filter that keeps them out.
A lot of the people we **say** we want in office could earn more in the private sector. Because the market rewards skill, scarcity, and momentum. And Congress does not just pay you. It pulls you out of your career.
If you are a doctor, you are not just stepping away from income. You are stepping away from practice, from staying sharp, from continuing education, from the daily rhythm of your field. If you are an engineer, a founder, an executive, you are stepping away from an industry that moves fast and punishes gaps. "Congress" looks impressive on a resume in a political sense, but it can absolutely be a professional suicide for your actual discipline.
Now add the risk. You can serve two years and be done. You can serve four and lose. You can serve ten and get taken out by redistricting. Then you try to re-enter the market older, behind, and sometimes obsolete compared to the people who kept building while you were gone.
So we say we want younger people. We say we want skilled people. But we structure the job so that anyone with serious earning power has to take a leap that most rational people will not take.
#### The Two-Homes Reality
They have to maintain a life in the district they represent, and they need housing in Washington, D.C. when Congress is in session. There is no automatic "D.C. apartment allowance" that magically covers this. Yes, technically, a House member can use part of their congressional office budget to reimburse lodging tied to official business.
But that office budget is meant to fund staff, constituent services, travel, district offices, and the actual mechanics of doing the job. It was not designed to function as a personal housing subsidy.
So for most members, the reality is simple: maintaining two households is expensive, and Washington, D.C. is one of the most expensive housing markets in the country.
This is where the flat salary argument becomes lazy. A member from rural Ohio earns the same $174,000 base salary as a member from Manhattan. Those two people do not experience $174,000 the same way. It is not even close. Cost of living, spousal income, outside assets, and existing wealth all change how sustainable that salary is.
In practice, the flat salary quietly favors people who already have money, already have passive income, already have a high-earning spouse, or already have networks that make the lifestyle manageable.
If you want ordinary, talented people to serve, you cannot structure the job as if it is tailored for people who can already afford to serve.
I have said it before and I will say it again. $174,000 should be the base. But cost-of-living adjustments should exist, because the country is not one price.
#### The Temptation Problem Nobody Likes to Admit
The third issue is uncomfortable.
In Washington, you are surrounded by wealth. Lobbyists. Donors. Venture capitalists. CEOs. People who can make a quarter-million-dollar fundraising dinner feel like a normal affair.
I'm not saying Members should be competing with billionaires. **That 's not the point.** The point is that the environment creates pressure. It creates comparison. It creates rationalization. It creates a constant whisper in the background that says: you're doing a high-status job in a high-cost city while everyone around you is swimming in money.
So what do a lot of Members do?
They trade stocks. They chase book deals. They build personal brands. They line up their future. They network for the exit. They start thinking about cable news contracts and corporate boards while they are still in office, because they are already planning how to make the money they believe they are "leaving on the table."
This is one of the reasons stock trading reform keeps stalling. It is not the only reason, but it is part of the ecosystem. People justify ethically sketchy behavior by telling themselves they have to. They justify it as participating in the free market. They justify it as survival.
I disagree with that justification. But I understand the psychology that produces it.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/5463f0cf-6872-41e5-8f5b-e24450b5bfab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### Why Congress Does Not Fix It
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f79eee90-1a22-4ed7-a181-0950bb728f33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Congress has not meaningfully raised its pay because it is political suicide.
Congressional pay has been frozen at **$174,000 since 2009** , and while that number sounds large, the reality is that it has quietly lost a massive amount of purchasing power over the last decade and a half.
Adjusted for inflation, **$174,000 in 2009 would be roughly $258,000 in 2026 dollars** , meaning members of Congress today are operating with about 30 percent less real buying power than when the freeze began.
Stagnant pay does not eliminate money from politics, **it increases dependence on outside wealth, donors, lobbyists, and personal fortunes,** making Congress less accessible.
If Congress votes itself a raise, people lose their minds. The media loses its mind. Voters lose their minds. It becomes a story about greed, not about incentives, even when incentives are the entire problem.
So instead of fixing the front door, Congress leaves the side doors open.
They do not raise salaries, but they allow the ethical gray zones to persist. And then everyone acts shocked when people find ways to make up the difference.
#### A Compromise That Actually Makes Sense
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/56422401-719b-4526-abec-e81aad1b1ef3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Here is the trade I would make.
Pay Members more. Meaningfully more. Keep the base salary structure, but add cost-of-living adjustments. Meaning adjust the base salary to $258,000 a year which would be the same as $174,000 in 2009 adjusted for inflation. Then add a COLA or cost-of-living adjustments depending on the region or district they represent. Meaning that someone in Manhattan should be paid considerably more than somebody in Cleveland. Also, someone in Cleveland should probably make a little bit more than somebody in Mississippi or Alabama.
In exchange, ban stock trading. Full ban. No cute loopholes. No "spouse can trade." No "just a little." Require divestment or blind trusts with real enforcement and real penalties.
You want to serve? Fine. Serve. You are paid well enough to do it without justifying self-dealing.
That is a fair trade.
**Other Options I Would Consider**
One idea is a congressional housing complex. An opt-in residence in Washington, built and maintained by the government, with secure, high-quality apartments. A functional living solution that reduces the pressure of maintaining two residences.
Another idea is a more radical one. Pay Members the median income of their district while in office, plus necessary expenses, while housing is provided in DC. Then escrow the remaining salary and pay it out after they leave office.
For example, the median salary in Medina Ohio is $76,000 a year. A Congress person that represents that area should only be able to make $76,000 a year. However, considering their congressional salary, in my opinion, should be hundreds of thousands of dollars more than that, the rest goes into escrow until they are finished serving. After 10 years that could be a couple million dollars that you would happily give to them upon leaving office.
While you serve, you live like your constituents. When you leave, you are not financially punished for serving.
I'm not saying these are perfect. I'm saying we should be thinking like adults about incentives.
#### Why I'm Even Talking About This
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7d01dbe9-c2a1-4a4d-9631-b4ffb2f02885?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Congressional Stock Trades](https://substack.com/redirect/06677838-792e-45ff-9619-c2e70df85e5a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Because underpayment breeds resentment.
It helps justify unethical behavior. It pushes talented people away. It encourages a Congress built out of wealthy retirees, professional politicians, and people whose real job is fundraising and positioning for their next gig.
If we want Congress to act like public servants, we have to structure public service like we actually value it, and then we have to tighten the ethical rules like we mean it.
What are your thoughts?

Please consider sharing and subscribing to fuel the ANGER for change. What 15 years of stagnant pay really incentivized. | | | Feb 13 | | | | | | | | | | | | Here's an unpopular opinion I didn't say out loud when I was running for office, but I'll say it now. | | ---|---|--- Members of Congress do not get paid enough. Yes, I know the number. The base salary for most Members is $174,000 a year. And yes, compared to the median American household, that is a serious salary. I'm not pretending otherwise. But once you step back and look at what we claim we want out of Congress, who we claim we want to recruit, and what incentives we've built into the job, the current pay structure helps produce the exact problems everyone complains about. This is not a sympathy post for politicians. This is a post about incentives. The Competition Problem If we genuinely want Congress to include more ambitious, capable, working-age professionals, the current salary often functions like a filter that keeps them out. A lot of the people we say we want in office could earn more in the private sector. Because the market rewards skill, scarcity, and momentum. And Congress does not just pay you. It pulls you out of your career. If you are a doctor, you are not just stepping away from income. You are stepping away from practice, from staying sharp, from continuing education, from the daily rhythm of your field. If you are an engineer, a founder, an executive, you are stepping away from an industry that moves fast and punishes gaps. "Congress" looks impressive on a resume in a political sense, but it can absolutely be a professional suicide for your actual discipline. Now add the risk. You can serve two years and be done. You can serve four and lose. You can serve ten and get taken out by redistricting. Then you try to re-enter the market older, behind, and sometimes obsolete compared to the people who kept building while you were gone. So we say we want younger people. We say we want skilled people. But we structure the job so that anyone with serious earning power has to take a leap that most rational people will not take. The Two-Homes Reality They have to maintain a life in the district they represent, and they need housing in Washington, D.C. when Congress is in session. There is no automatic "D.C. apartment allowance" that magically covers this. Yes, technically, a House member can use part of their congressional office budget to reimburse lodging tied to official business. But that office budget is meant to fund staff, constituent services, travel, district offices, and the actual mechanics of doing the job. It was not designed to function as a personal housing subsidy. So for most members, the reality is simple: maintaining two households is expensive, and Washington, D.C. is one of the most expensive housing markets in the country. This is where the flat salary argument becomes lazy. A member from rural Ohio earns the same $174,000 base salary as a member from Manhattan. Those two people do not experience $174,000 the same way. It is not even close. Cost of living, spousal income, outside assets, and existing wealth all change how sustainable that salary is. In practice, the flat salary quietly favors people who already have money, already have passive income, already have a high-earning spouse, or already have networks that make the lifestyle manageable. If you want ordinary, talented people to serve, you cannot structure the job as if it is tailored for people who can already afford to serve. I have said it before and I will say it again. $174,000 should be the base. But cost-of-living adjustments should exist, because the country is not one price. The Temptation Problem Nobody Likes to Admit The third issue is uncomfortable. In Washington, you are surrounded by wealth. Lobbyists. Donors. Venture capitalists. CEOs. People who can make a quarter-million-dollar fundraising dinner feel like a normal affair. I'm not saying Members should be competing with billionaires. That 's not the point. The point is that the environment creates pressure. It creates comparison. It creates rationalization. It creates a constant whisper in the background that says: you're doing a high-status job in a high-cost city while everyone around you is swimming in money. So what do a lot of Members do? They trade stocks. They chase book deals. They build personal brands. They line up their future. They network for the exit. They start thinking about cable news contracts and corporate boards while they are still in office, because they are already planning how to make the money they believe they are "leaving on the table." This is one of the reasons stock trading reform keeps stalling. It is not the only reason, but it is part of the ecosystem. People justify ethically sketchy behavior by telling themselves they have to. They justify it as participating in the free market. They justify it as survival. I disagree with that justification. But I understand the psychology that produces it. Why Congress Does Not Fix It | | ---|---|--- Congress has not meaningfully raised its pay because it is political suicide. Congressional pay has been frozen at $174,000 since 2009 , and while that number sounds large, the reality is that it has quietly lost a massive amount of purchasing power over the last decade and a half. Adjusted for inflation, $174,000 in 2009 would be roughly $258,000 in 2026 dollars , meaning members of Congress today are operating with about 30 percent less real buying power than when the freeze began. Stagnant pay does not eliminate money from politics, it increases dependence on outside wealth, donors, lobbyists, and personal fortunes, making Congress less accessible. If Congress votes itself a raise, people lose their minds. The media loses its mind. Voters lose their minds. It becomes a story about greed, not about incentives, even when incentives are the entire problem. So instead of fixing the front door, Congress leaves the side doors open. They do not raise salaries, but they allow the ethical gray zones to persist. And then everyone acts shocked when people find ways to make up the difference. A Compromise That Actually Makes Sense | | ---|---|--- Here is the trade I would make. Pay Members more. Meaningfully more. Keep the base salary structure, but add cost-of-living adjustments. Meaning adjust the base salary to $258,000 a year which would be the same as $174,000 in 2009 adjusted for inflation. Then add a COLA or cost-of-living adjustments depending on the region or district they represent. Meaning that someone in Manhattan should be paid considerably more than somebody in Cleveland. Also, someone in Cleveland should probably make a little bit more than somebody in Mississippi or Alabama. In exchange, ban stock trading. Full ban. No cute loopholes. No "spouse can trade." No "just a little." Require divestment or blind trusts with real enforcement and real penalties. You want to serve? Fine. Serve. You are paid well enough to do it without justifying self-dealing. That is a fair trade. Other Options I Would Consider One idea is a congressional housing complex. An opt-in residence in Washington, built and maintained by the government, with secure, high-quality apartments. A functional living solution that reduces the pressure of maintaining two residences. Another idea is a more radical one. Pay Members the median income of their district while in office, plus necessary expenses, while housing is provided in DC. Then escrow the remaining salary and pay it out after they leave office. For example, the median salary in Medina Ohio is $76,000 a year. A Congress person that represents that area should only be able to make $76,000 a year. However, considering their congressional salary, in my opinion, should be hundreds of thousands of dollars more than that, the rest goes into escrow until they are finished serving. After 10 years that could be a couple million dollars that you would happily give to them upon leaving office. While you serve, you live like your constituents. When you leave, you are not financially punished for serving. I'm not saying these are perfect. I'm saying we should be thinking like adults about incentives. Why I'm Even Talking About This | | ---|---|--- Because underpayment breeds resentment. It helps justify unethical behavior. It pushes talented people away. It encourages a Congress built out of wealthy retirees, professional politicians, and people whose real job is fundraising and positioning for their next gig. If we want Congress to act like public servants, we have to structure public service like we actually value it, and then we have to tighten the ethical rules like we mean it. Grand Junction and Pueblo, CO: Prominent Second Amendment advocate Kyle Rittenhouse has officially endorsed Hope Scheppelman for U.S. Congress in Colorado's 3rd Congressional District (CD-3), citing the urgent need for unapologetic constitutional leadership in Washington.

Scheppelman has been a leading voice at the Colorado State Capitol opposing unconstitutional overreach, fighting sweeping firearm restrictions that target responsible citizens instead of criminals.
"The Second Amendment is not conditional. It is not negotiable. I am a Second Amendment absolutist," said Hope Scheppelman. "Our rights come from God, not government. In the U.S. Congress, I will defend those rights without hesitation and without apology."
"Our Founders were clear," Scheppelman added. "An armed citizenry is essential to a free nation. The right to keep and bear arms is a safeguard against tyranny, and I will protect it."

Dear Peter, I’d like to have an honest conversation with you about Alaska. I believe our future is bright and our best days are ahead of us as a state and country. **That’s why I'm running to be Alaska's next governor.** As lieutenant governor, I’ve fought tough battles for Alaskans. As Commissioner of Corrections, I fought to repeal soft-on-crime laws _and won_. And in the state legislature, I went up against politicians in Juneau to protect the PFD _and won_. I promise to bring the same grit and common sense to the Governor’s office, because I want to ensure Alaska remains the best place to live, work, and raise a family for our kids and grandkids. ↓My Alaska story starts at 18. I came up for a two-week summer trip and ended up staying to work on a pipeline. I loved the attitude here. It was rugged, independent, full of American spirit, neighborly, and welcoming. Every day was a new adventure, so I decided to stay and build a life, career, and family here. After working in several different industries, I was encouraged to run for office by my community. From serving nine years in the Legislature to stepping up as Commissioner of Corrections and now as your Lieutenant Governor, I’ve always kept my word and put Alaskans first above party politics and political pressure. _**That’s how you have to lead in Alaska:
with _grit_ and the _resolve_ to do the right thing.**_ As governor, I’ll focus on what matters most:
* _**Protecting**_ the PFD for families today and tomorrow
* Growing jobs and _**strengthening**_ our economy
* Supporting resource development to _**lower costs**_ and achieve energy independence
* Backing law enforcement and _**keeping our communities safe**_
* Balancing budgets and _**cutting waste**_
* Building _**strong schools**_ and preparing students for the future.

Alaska gave me everything, and I vow to continue giving back. Now that you know my story, I hope to hear yours over the next year. Today, I am hopeful that you will take two minutes to become a part of our [**leadership team**](http://links.mail.nancyforalaska.com/u/click?_t=070db738c7d848a188c7a9e8a29f1bde&_m=963e89fd264f46319c0b1c92840214f4&_e=fOVQRYEEORD2BJvejd8Ro7kY9jhqPPjCuh_h89BvvGNUFijO8t72VXdS6WJtqWe58rBjw7P6eBGEhO7umrXrQebm3XQOQ1BOJWKMYAmfj1I7tb1Zeiyv36d0kZQdEJkMzc6wAEF-1g70j40XBxlvnHlmYRP100rAWXM0wdB07GraVCyh2sKThjCCUJhmCAboOmbPe6UPFvJb5C7r-cnk4sSMJ65YRbGmVD6r1KiNcqs7qvn0uGDu_A8jPX85RhpWlW-jgMuxpS2opif1-Z7xVcbEWFgZ7kajbOEidy1TFFAwY8R0mic0HZCe2fWs7Paxzy2D2kh7XSgg-PjZgY8DbWJQXBzJqSxtsHLJ6OzabKbccPtpuRamf18sDpzNnC6XeL9CBnw2oeziBUg4Z6gml0ZKSjanK6ifH_Zw6j4_Gau8F78o0Lh55c3M_svF98ulUvWzDbcRDXrGTyOh-MMxTsD2EzHvs0FBwxfyUsY3o4eWv_H4LCW9ZkTBVmhuFQHfJxPaSvKGq5lAmwY4b4X25HELdeCnYQXx0p2sv4sMY624irCctNLdUBEf0GHNLWefuOoyZn653vYdtq22SO-3GyiqR1-lLPiBWYFh4V4yfi68pbFHpyIDCxrZpDyMZebqCszd8HHaVzL2kdWsHL_k45NSoZUxV7sSu7tGGZlFbm_M5XWzFCKVcIqof2tpSawJlVJbm7LxG4xOUXxxi-pTz8YMr2-b_SlY1QwTfPWGgv10p1LJ15ogu3apDotRNVzbe8ONxEGADbQwC2kqYpwxChD2_ltGimPLt2BbTMnQE_yb8doDK99u3JT2lC_7HpnA_lF12827nZJP_f242Xc0plqWF9dVELfJedK3y-SDs8ptl3zPYWwZnxG-xgkW9nnFL_F5FwmfPaoYoXNLqiKgsZ17jn73Mn7cjuhBmOPjUnQaoftxD51fICAr9zRAkTmrgvQpC4mz2Qpi6hRqrgFA4eqo5UxC6XXfesPgzsP2xVI5MnQ27788xUfwYJPPwGSVVgDYLFIKCiUceaR0rB03QtAacXOOIqf_-iJsmwqNa1bN0ENIayMPifyk-ecBWFblWLI8fLH-iN_VITqFMEVt-5M99BJ5zISh6vQMHRkrN_2TDx1jov7W6w-nhEBfZs7XNjqld0Fp-lPWYIkPhv8suqGenkzNgWZCjCJV_fLzwH4XBIWAoOmDahTfblz8PtXWqac1zqbOgyY2J3KgKNwK_pgJBxLIQayda8b8TVnBfIDyZnCO2ZlNGOjVwzBJ9w1VSGpR8B2kaDnHp0k9gy9nDcsYdj8tTFH91aqxliFmkgQQq08RZeopFlo0lsY8vkxPrwCUNrsvyq_qlNBzzsK9i1D5k4TdFl4bReQFZJfDJ_nL6n8TbBSZIIchkHOzyRLDDsG_9A3zw-0mm6Z9qYLGVFP7p3S2LEvDa9ldiXuhfeHAN1umYmDU88X2iHQrtD9CyL0WOlSQeqXBWnoUIDhfM6SDSsh-tltrV2uB26aiIijKm8VjneqjbUO-OkzAugYia-axcqIhOiwtdu0B3UYwZpKr9QqSbDdqrllT8on0VwIFtWAEsqqQuKz-9MoSxXFX) with a small or large financial contribution. clean_body: An important message about the future of our state and country.| | | Click here if you wish to unsubscribe Dear Peter, I’d like to have an honest conversation with you about Alaska. I believe our future is bright and our best days are ahead of us as a state and country. That’s why I'm running to be Alaska's next governor. As lieutenant governor, I’ve fought tough battles for Alaskans. As Commissioner of Corrections, I fought to repeal soft-on-crime laws and won. And in the state legislature, I went up against politicians in Juneau to protect the PFD and won. I promise to bring the same grit and common sense to the Governor’s office, because I want to ensure Alaska remains the best place to live, work, and raise a family for our kids and grandkids. If that’s enough for you, please join my by supporting me . If you’d like to read more of my story, check it out below! ↓My Alaska story starts at 18. I came up for a two-week summer trip and ended up staying to work on a pipeline. I loved the attitude here. It was rugged, independent, full of American spirit, neighborly, and welcoming. Every day was a new adventure, so I decided to stay and build a life, career, and family here. After working in several different industries, I was encouraged to run for office by my community. From serving nine years in the Legislature to stepping up as Commissioner of Corrections and now as your Lieutenant Governor, I’ve always kept my word and put Alaskans first above party politics and political pressure. That’s how you have to lead in Alaska: with grit and the resolve to do the right thing. As governor, I’ll focus on what matters most: Protecting the PFD for families today and tomorrow Growing jobs and strengthening our economy Supporting resource development to lower costs and achieve energy independence Backing law enforcement and keeping our communities safe Balancing budgets and cutting waste Building strong schools and preparing students for the future. Alaska gave me everything, and I vow to continue giving back. Now that you know my story, I hope to hear yours over the next year. Today, I am hopeful that you will take two minutes to become a part of our with a small or large financial contribution. Whatever fits your budget! I’d be honored to have your support. Together, we will build a stronger future for Alaska. With gratitude, Nancy Dahlstrom Alaska's Lt. Governor and 2026 Republican candidate for governor | | | | ---|---

## State Seeks Info on Data Center Water Usage
The Texas Public Utility Commission (PUC) is sending surveys to the state's data centers and cryptomining facilities to [collect information](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0Muq20AMgOGnGe8UZhRf4oUX2Xh3CqXQLo1syfHA2BPmkjl5-xL3EboTCMT_6c_X9EXW2ePxg3YZ0vfqp0NKdJKShIkp0SJHklAoSciRHsKSAk2osQWNYK4Tk3Xvqa54mDX3ppLBdJ3ub7Wp22ob-n5uGmrNzKJZ2DR1c7tJ1yMuTXPFtbLD55hGczWoEfFSMzbrrTPcy0xtP6taC9vkwyVtkuSb4ure_iXhsvi9csOW0jOq613hqHAspVz2eHx2Ckc5IEeF4welcDznzRfY87LBiQL2QBY-VPhnjZCjAMEhBWIOL3nD4rNj2MQ94QyAII_sKPkQYbUHg89J4UgB7nfz-yf_0lUY-Fmscza2nar1YyfrzuD0f29-Dfg3AAD__yqgk70) about their water usage. The surveys must be completed within six weeks, and the PUC will produce a report on the findings by the end of this year. Data centers and cryptomining operations use water directly to cool their servers and indirectly through the electricity they consume. A recent study by the Houston Advanced Research Center suggests data centers could account for about 3% of the state's water usage by 2030. "_We want those jobs. We need those jobs_ ," said State Rep. Armando Walle (D-Houston), who [authored the budget rider](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAMgJ8mbEGJSUkZMvwLW__1RmQaA1FTUiVuad_-BKd7gps8WP7k7_u6DBcMMazzf7yT4_eUhpW2EomZ8uCR8UorU96QKT8LzuSJMw6goJUKpG4GjyF-BlN5Nyrf6YqctlZ1Z6NNWy0OvfVXf5rIIjRaKWNP1DVt02hrLcBYBbfDFOhGgwKA2ng4TWerfUcjtt0ojCIfOOWaF2J6Y5niJ70o19d0r6JbmB9FNP8E9AL6bdvq2xvXfSmg320E9MfZ75SZ5mdETrnILcQosdzk7ip_ZIvkJEeawyozPVLmsM6SFwpZHh3kEUJAX2XnHzshlNYKo-Y7hnh8xX9r-XLwHQAA__-0NYtq) to fund the survey. "_However, we also have to be very good stewards of our water resources_." On Tuesday, Hood County commissioners [rejected](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO5CoQxvHT4IwWFBhM4OAlzualG1plKLqRsLGAHk_ffuXdI2xc0l_1_X59rV-Ycjqe_-NOc_-JZT3oapl6p7oG7Ojp6FQv7FTfDZ8UqFdcQYDhArhUa8CUP6sewryJ4ORAs7RWuElLbYbXPIJEr8cxorEKDWjEzVulovGbgi0Oab5jAqSSIADgoQOMcbIyONrQuI1pQSH1Uh_9RZ1-sMX8Kd9UH77sQ55fvZ-Nqf8YLAyW67oeV0S8jwwWrD35TAyWexeDJRePmcHyKiVwX95H_3Bf9j21lspBtfHznTM_azlLo8D3UrGXmt47vzn4X4-7BJPlgkAoYzRHN0quI47cWWW5s9qhoMnFSQ51DueVck7NWKbFc8eU__ze_038e4bfAQAA__8expT6) a moratorium on new data centers after two state legislators penned an open letter [arguing](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8Gb4ngQXAYGNrBWzpV6mg94DlBwnYEL4nz95X7C13vcO695-cyXjCXvFy_cCbP27SOC71aIWaqY0LGSAtTfSFTfTS8UiKuOIIEe5BwUHpMmMt7NF3yQSanOvKq76U7G2Vsd_PTKWIIU690b0KAEKONMZ20mZxyZF2X_Q6ToLQCCQBHk-A0nXuVHAW0LggjKWVe65FvxLRhm8p7fVI9xnXuir8x35vQHwIGAcO2pwKGb8L5c7-xxPVRWcDQGPnRBAywl4EGqd3ZgtynddWn-yuXkpvthZHXGXP54_P_rDw9_AYAAP__sgJ01g) they lacked constitutional authority to enact one.
## Texans Connected to Jeffrey Epstein
Several prominent Texans [have been connected to](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGOwyAUBNDT4M4WfGNjFxTbuMu2W1oYPjErAhb8xMntV8kVthtppDfS_FzWiwkxpOu3uaGmp89rwrNGJMKyOkPGYiIspyEs92qu6JCKWYHD2HJoRb86E-JrlY3TG3ezaFALpfg8SSHHZtdTrwbhPAAM8yCF805ufpabEHaYlJ2aoN8YB9EL4ADQSQeDn5RwM25mnDcmObpAuXS0I-HTVB9f-YGls_nWRL0THZX1XwwWBst5np3dS07vlsFi75HuBRksplCw8Z1-0fuCrxaPShhS-0Fbm1NCSyGn2oLopRLD1B370RTtjjPEGOqomOTXmwnxs03_e-yh4S8AAP__gYSAxw) financier and child sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein, according to records of correspondence released by the Department of Justice. The late Ken Starr, the former president of Baylor University and the independent counsel who investigated President Bill Clinton during the Monica Lewinsky scandal, helped Epstein secure the 2008 plea deal that enabled him to avoid federal sex trafficking charges. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. name: Office of U.S. Senator Angela Alsobrooks
subject: Senator Alsobrooks Newsletter -- February 13, 2026
body:
|

---
Dear Friends and Neighbors,

Our nation has been under siege by masked federal ICE agents who have been violating our civil rights, harassing Americans, and those who have committed no crimes. As you know, children have been swept up in these raids and exposed to the violence that ICE has been perpetrating across cities. As a result, Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and I, along with Representative Mike Quigley (D-Ill.), led more than 55 colleagues in pressing HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. on this escalating violence which threatens to leave our children with lasting physical and psychological trauma. Under the Trump administration, children - both U.S. citizens and noncitizens - have been exposed to increasingly violent and intense immigration enforcement operations. After Donald Trump rescinded ICE's sensitive locations policy on day one, ICE has carried out raids at schools, day care centers - and even a child's birthday party. Even when children are not the direct target, their exposure to this violence can create lasting trauma. Five-year-old Minnesota resident Liam Ramos was detained for more than a week in a Texas facility after reportedly being used as "bait" to capture his father. Liam's father [said](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15567.16291567.5935525.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.cnn.com%2f2026%2f01%2f31%2fus%2fliam-ramos-judge-release-ice-detention&redir_log=095011150778492) Liam was not eating well and was sleeping a lot and asking about his mother and classmates. In Massachusetts, a man suffered an apparent seizure while ICE agents attempted to detain his wife as their toddler cried within arm's reach. Witnesses allege agents pushed him, struck him, and pressed on his neck while the child remained trapped between the adults. In Illinois, ICE agents forcibly detained a day care teacher in front of her students. In another incident, masked agents deployed tear gas near an elementary school in Chicago, sending children running and teachers scrambling for cover. In Texas, ICE agents stormed a five-year-old child's birthday party, where state and federal officers conducted an operation that resulted in the apprehension of 47 people, including nine minors - one of whom was just three years old. ICE operations are also hurting children's academic and social development. In districts where ICE raids have occurred, schools are reporting declining student attendance and performance; in some schools, nearly half of students have been absent following school-based ICE raids. Early childhood providers have reported attrition from day care, after-school programs, and other community programs that typically serve as spaces for positive socialization, mental health counseling, and other forms of support. Immigration enforcement actions are also impacting children's access to health care. Most health care workers report significant or moderate decreases in patient visits since January 2025; for the children that do continue to visit the doctor, they reportedly have declining physical and mental health. One doctor observed "abnormal weight gain trajectories" in children not getting exercise outdoors due to "fear of encountering ICE," and another pediatrician reported that "minors [are] constantly crying during their well-child checks expressing their fear for themselves and their families." ICE and CBP's disregard for child welfare undermines the government's core obligation to protect children. As a result, we are demanding to receive any data on the impact of immigration operations on children's health and development. It's important that we safeguard our children's wellbeing - they are our future. We cannot let another penny go to this murderous goon squad without serious reforms and guardrails. I have voted no on increased funding and will continue to do so.

**Fighting Against RFK Jr. 's Corruption ** As you may be aware, prior to his appointment as HHS secretary, RFK Jr. had a lucrative career in the anti-vaccine litigation industry. Secretary Kennedy, his family, and Wisner Baum - the law firm he previously worked with - have made millions by referring and representing claimants before Vaccine Injury Compensation Program (VICP). In July, Secretary Kennedy announced that he was working with the Department of Justice and Attorney General Pam Bondi to "fix" the vaccine court. Last month, Secretary Kennedy fired at least half of the expert members of the Advisory Commission on Childhood Vaccines (ACCV), which makes recommendations to inform the VICP - shortly after he unilaterally overhauled the childhood vaccine schedule. Further VICP changes reportedly under consideration, including making certain medical injuries with no ties to vaccines compensable, would likely lead to vaccine shortages, endanger public health, and could enrich Secretary Kennedy's immediate family and close allies. Republicans are making people with Medicare who take these life-saving drugs pay more for them.
27. As states scramble to implement Republicans' Medicaid cuts - the largest in history - Kennedy provided cold comfort to states when he announced that [Medicaid vendors would provide some discounted services to states to implement these draconian cuts](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15567.16291567.5935525.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.healthcaredive.com%2fnews%2fmedicaid-vendors-trump-deals-cms-work-requirements%2f810839%2f&redir_log=194285243723642). States must pay hundreds of millions of dollars to these middlemen to update their systems so that Americans will be tied up in the Big Ugly Bill's new red tape restrictions. Many of these companies already have a [proven track record of system errors](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15567.16291567.5935525.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fkffhealthnews.org%2fnews%2farticle%2fdeloitte-contractors-medicaid-eligibility-system-errors-senators%2f&redir_log=329548851098741) that have wrongly ripped health insurance away from eligible new mothers, people with disabilities, and other working people.

**In the Community **

Howard County has made its stance clear: when it comes to ICE's inhumane detention centers, the answer is no and hell no. I was proud to join County Executive Calvin Ball as he signed emergency legislation revoking the building permit for a privately owned ICE detention facility whose owners attempted to subvert state law.

As a former Prince George's County State's Attorney, it was great to meet with State's Attorneys from across Maryland alongside Senator Chis Van Hollen. We discussed supporting victims, the opioid crisis, online child safety, and addressing workforce challenges in prosecutors' offices.
I was honored to join the National Black Nurses Association Day on Capitol Hill. Their advocacy for patients, equity, and a stronger nursing workforce is powerful and it's being heard. I'm proud to stand with these professionals in this fight for equity in health care.

I was grateful to participate in the Congressional Research Service (CRS) speaker series. The talented staff at CRS provides vital non-partisan research to Members of Congress. I would like to thank the entire CRS team for all they do!

Last Sunday, I had the privilege of attending a wonderful service and sermon for Divine 9 Day at Greater Mt. Nebo AME Church. Guest speaker Rev. Dr. Gwendolyn Boyd delivered a powerful message about the strength in unity.

**Fighting Through Legislation **

It's been a busy few weeks here in Washington, and I continue to fight for Marylanders through legislation. From protecting your privacy from agencies like ICE and CBP, to legislation that seeks to make public the financial impact mass firings have had on state and local governments, I am working every day to demand transparency and fairness on your behalf.
_Below are the bills I have introduced the last couple of weeks_ :

National Council on African American History and Culture Act of 2026: This bill would establish a 12-member advisory council within the National Endowment for the Humanities dedicated to preserving, promoting, and interpreting African American history and culture. Appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate, the Council will be composed of experts, scholars, and leaders in African American humanities and cultural preservation. The Council will evaluate federal humanities programs, gather information on historical and cultural trends, develop policy recommendations, and submit annual reports to guide national efforts to support African American history and culture. The Council will sunset ten years after enactment.

Fiscal Harms of Federal Firings Act: This bill would direct the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to conduct a comprehensive study of the financial impacts of the Trump Administration's mass firings on state and local governments.
_Below are bills I cosponsored_ :

ICE Out of My Face Act: This bill would ban U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) from using facial recognition technology and other biometric recognition tactics. The bill also includes strong privacy measures to ensure all data collected for such systems is deleted and provisions to allow individuals to seek civil penalties for violations.

Rebuild America's Schools Act (RASA): This bill would address the need to modernize school facilities by investing $130 billion targeted at high-poverty schools with facilities that pose health and safety risks to students and staff, it would also invest in improving broadband and Wi-Fi in public schools

Saving Lives and Taxpayer Dollars Act: This bill would prevent the unnecessary destruction and waste of foreign assistance commodities, including food, medicine, and medical devices. It would ensure that they are delivered to intended recipients before they spoil or expire, prohibit the destruction of any such commodities unless the government has already exhausted all options to sell or donate them, and require reporting to Congress on any destroyed foreign assistance commodities.

Federal Adjustment of Income Rates (FAIR) Act: This bill would provide federal employees with a 4.3% raise in calendar year 2026. This includes 3.3% raises under the statutory pay systems and for prevailing rate employees, and a 1% increase to locality pay.

The EQIP Improvement Act of 2025: This bipartisan bill would reduce the overall payment cap on EQIP contracts, reduce federal cost-sharing for practices that provide little or no environmental benefits, and eliminate a requirement that 50% of EQIP funding flow to livestock operators. To make the Environmental Quality Incentive Program more effective, this bill would re-focus support towards farmers and ranchers who need it the most by targeting funding to more producers and prioritizing conservation practices with significantly greater environmental and water quality benefits. This bill will eliminate wasteful spending and give states more control over conservation efforts.

Insurance Fraud Accountability Act: This legislation would amend the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to crack down on fraudulent enrollments and plan changes in Affordable Care Act Marketplace coverage. It establishes civil and criminal penalties for agents and brokers who submit false or fraudulent information, requires a consent verification process for new enrollments and coverage changes, and increases oversight of marketing organizations and enrollment patterns.

A resolution supporting the designation of 2026 as the "International Year of the Woman Farmer" to recognize and honor the critical role of women in agriculture. (Passed the Senate!)

A resolution designating January 23, 2026, as "Maternal Health Awareness Day".

A resolution celebrating the 40th anniversary of the International Coastal Cleanup.

A resolution calling upon the United States and Russia to "continue to respect the numerical constraints on the strategic deployed nuclear forces established by the New START Treaty until such time as a new nuclear arms control framework is established."

A joint resolution to overturn a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) rule that bans abortion counseling and abortion care for veterans and their dependents, including in cases of rape, incest, or serious health risk. The rule reinstates a near-total prohibition on reproductive health services within the VA, reversing a policy that allowed limited access to abortion care in medical emergencies and cases of sexual violence.

A resolution condemning Russian incursions into NATO territory and reaffirming Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty.

**Stay in the Fight ** I know these are difficult times. But please know that I will continue fighting for you every step of the way. We will not give up. We will not give in to this Administration, and I ask that you continue to fight alongside us. Please continue to reach out to us. You can call the office or connect with us at [alsobrooks.senate.gov](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15567.16291567.5935525.7190525&report_id=&redirect=http%3a%2f%2falsobrooks.senate.gov%2f&redir_log=346519414955204). You can also follow us on Bluesky, Instagram, Facebook, Threads, YouTube, and X. We are in this TOGETHER. Sincerely, Angela D. Alsobrooks
United States Senator

Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635.
