Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

| Letter from the Chair

The Big Tent of Nebraska Republicans: United by Enduring Values
The Nebraska Republican Party represents a true cross-section of our state-- a majority of Nebraskans who come from every corner of conservative thought. We include ideological purists and pragmatic problem-solvers, social moderates and fiscal hawks, corporatists and populists, neoconservatives and non-interventionists. A small but vocal fringe may push to tear things down and divide, but the vast majority of us are committed to building up.
America's two-party system has long served as a healthy balance--a yin and yang of ideas that checks extremes and drives progress. Yet coalitions shift when the balance is disrupted, as we've seen in recent years.
Unchecked illegal immigration and shifts to social and ideologic extremes, heavily promoted by the opposition, has suppressed wages, limited job advancement, fractured our social contract, and strained communities. As a result, the Republican Party is increasingly attracting conservative youth, organized labor, working families of varying socio-economic means, and growing numbers of people of color who no longer vote in rigid blocs. These new voices are enriching our party--and naturally sparking healthy debate as we refine our shared identity.
This disruption is a sign of growth, not weakness. By returning to our core values and principles, we find our common ground and our guiding North Star. Let the love of Truth, Justice, and Mercy continue to guide our most noble ideals and our daily interactions with each other.
Any statement of who we are as Republicans must begin with our constitutional duty to protect God-given individual liberties. It must affirm our commitment to strengthening families, dramatically improving educational outcomes for every child, ensuring safe communities and abundant job opportunities, rooting out fraud and corruption, practicing sound fiscal responsibility, caring for the most vulnerable among us, and steadfastly defending the sanctity of innocent life.
Yes, Republicans will argue and debate--that's the nature of a vibrant, big-tent party. But to those watching from the outside: let them see a party that fights for something worth fighting for.
We are united in our devotion to freedom, opportunity, family, faith, and the Nebraska way of life. Together, we will continue to lead our state forward, defending these timeless principles and earning the trust of every Nebraskan who shares them.
Let's keep the conversation going, stay engaged, and stand strong--because Nebraska's future depends on it.

Sincerely, Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

| From the desk of Jeanne Reigle....
As we mark Day 24 of the legislative session, fiscal responsibility is in the spotlight. With a projected budget shortfall on the horizon, there's a strong push for spending restraint and smart reforms to keep Nebraska's finances healthy.
The NEGOP appreciates the solid work from our Republican senators. Hats off to Senator Lippincott for his bills to lower property valuations and improve TEEOSA (the school funding formula). Speaker Arch's LB1071, introduced on behalf of Governor Pillen, brings thoughtful fund management, spending cuts and real fiscal controls. Senator Murman's LB1244 eliminates some sales tax exemptions to help broaden the tax base. We also appreciate Senator Dover's LB990 for better credit distribution under the School District Property Tax Relief Act, and Senator Sorrentino's LB749, focused on updating tax levy calculations for municipal state aid. These bills are directly tackling fiscal responsibility, and there are plenty more that support the cause in indirect ways.
On the flip side, some state Democratic senators have been using procedural moves, strong opposition, amendments, and even symbolic gestures--like not standing for the Pledge of Allegiance or for teachers honored during Governor Pillen's State of the State address--to slow things down.
That's why getting (and staying) involved as conservatives is more important than ever! Grassroots involvement such as contacting your senator, submitting online comments on bills, and building support among friends and neighbors bolster our Republican senators. Your public testimony also really makes a difference--it strengthens our Republican senator's positions, shows real grassroots support from folks back home, and encourages moderates to stick with the conservative majority. A huge thank you to Eric Underwood, Danna Seevers, and Tom Nesbitt for testifying recently in the Revenue Committee and the Banking, Commerce and Insurance Committee.
Let's stay involved and keep the momentum going for a fiscally responsible Nebraska!

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair The Big Tent of Nebraska Republicans: United by Enduring Values The Nebraska Republican Party represents a true cross-section of our state-- a majority of Nebraskans who come from every corner of conservative thought. We include ideological purists and pragmatic problem-solvers, social moderates and fiscal hawks, corporatists and populists, neoconservatives and non-interventionists. A small but vocal fringe may push to tear things down and divide, but the vast majority of us are committed to building up. America's two-party system has long served as a healthy balance--a yin and yang of ideas that checks extremes and drives progress. Yet coalitions shift when the balance is disrupted, as we've seen in recent years. Unchecked illegal immigration and shifts to social and ideologic extremes, heavily promoted by the opposition, has suppressed wages, limited job advancement, fractured our social contract, and strained communities. As a result, the Republican Party is increasingly attracting conservative youth, organized labor, working families of varying socio-economic means, and growing numbers of people of color who no longer vote in rigid blocs. These new voices are enriching our party--and naturally sparking healthy debate as we refine our shared identity. This disruption is a sign of growth, not weakness. By returning to our core values and principles, we find our common ground and our guiding North Star. Let the love of Truth, Justice, and Mercy continue to guide our most noble ideals and our daily interactions with each other. Any statement of who we are as Republicans must begin with our constitutional duty to protect God-given individual liberties. It must affirm our commitment to strengthening families, dramatically improving educational outcomes for every child, ensuring safe communities and abundant job opportunities, rooting out fraud and corruption, practicing sound fiscal responsibility, caring for the most vulnerable among us, and steadfastly defending the sanctity of innocent life. Yes, Republicans will argue and debate--that's the nature of a vibrant, big-tent party. But to those watching from the outside: let them see a party that fights for something worth fighting for. We are united in our devotion to freedom, opportunity, family, faith, and the Nebraska way of life. You know, only about 45,000 of the 16 million brave Americans who fought in World War II are still with us.

This sponsored message from American Action News is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2ze614nqhgtmcp3gk0s3e8119u5en09lq3vkh5f40_rp22sh2s8i6epr4c1g6aor1c5h2bs)

| | Dear Fellow American,

How are you doing today?

You know, only about 45,000 of the 16 million brave Americans who fought in World War II are still with us. The efforts of those men did so much to shape our world today, and understanding World War II helps us to honor their sacrifices.

That's why Hillsdale College produced the free online course "**The Second World Wars.** "

In this course, you'll learn from historian **Victor Davis Hanson** as he teaches you how the conflict's many theaters, belligerents, operations, and tactics eventually came to define a single war. You'll examine the key investments, strategies, and leaders that led the Allied powers to victory over the Axis.

Nearly a quarter of a million people have signed up for this course already! Because so many have enjoyed this course, we put it all together in a handsome DVD box set for you.

As a thank-you for your generous gift of $100 or more to Hillsdale College, we'll send **" The Second World Wars" DVD box** **set** directly to your home--while supplies last second.

**If you want, you can claim your copy through this secure link:**

[**https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/support-the-second-world-wars**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zqofsjph3ce43nvt4cvf9eecfmufer0i3rlgk9o0_rp22sh2s8i6epr4c1g6aor1c5h2bs)

Thank you for helping us **reach** and **teach** future generations of Americans about liberty, faith, and character with us--including about World War II.

Best regards,

Bill Gray '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

**P.S.** The **" The Second World Wars" **DVD set is an excellent addition to a homeschool curriculum or for independent study. Plus, it's a perfect gift for anyone interested in learning more about the Second World War. If you'd like a copy, it can be yours for a gift of $100 or more, but the choice is yours--**[take a look and learn more!](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2za9bhdtr52nrje7p91sid8ffh50h3qeusf3m2nlg_rp22sh2s8i6epr4c1g6aor1c5h2bs)

The New York Times opinion piece published on December 21, 2025, titled something along the lines of "[After Mamdani's Win, the D.S.A. Has a High-Pressure Opportunity](https://substack.com/redirect/72e21008-e229-485c-8acb-be2e64ec58d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" or "Inside a Democratic Socialist Convention Galvanized by Mamdani's Big Win", offers an on-the-ground reflection from the [Democratic Socialists of America](https://substack.com/redirect/f75a8e5a-7283-4358-8cad-1713ffa610cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (DSA) national convention held in New Orleans.

The article captures a moment of triumph, introspection, and strategic urgency for the American left following Zohran Mamdani's stunning election as mayor of New York City in 2025.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.oNy3uVBXnJizct4NyVGmx2bf4f92ietqAzjjObEbgh8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=187854489)
The piece opens with a vivid scene from the convention floor in New Orleans, where DSA members are celebrating a banner year of electoral breakthroughs. The atmosphere is electric: attendees are energized by recent victories, chief among them Mamdani's ascent to the mayoralty of America's largest city. As a DSA member and state assemblyman-turned-mayor-elect (and later mayor), Mamdani's success is portrayed as a watershed moment that demonstrates democratic socialism is no longer a fringe or disqualifying label for many voters, especially amid soaring income inequality and widespread frustration with establishment politics.

The author describes how the DSA, though still tiny compared to the major parties, has grown significantly in influence and membership since the mid-2010s, fueled by figures like Bernie Sanders (a democratic socialist but not a formal DSA member), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (a prominent NYC DSA chapter member), and now Mamdani. The convention serves as a celebratory yet forward-looking gathering, where members savor wins but immediately pivot to the question of what comes next: how to capitalize on this momentum without squandering it.

A core theme is the "high-pressure opportunity" facing DSA. Mamdani's victory--defeating a heavyweight, albeit scandal ridden candidate, like former Gov. Andrew Cuomo in the Democratic primary and then winning the general election--proves that explicitly socialist candidates can win in major urban centers by focusing on bread-and-butter issues like housing affordability, universal childcare, free or reduced-cost public transit, and taxing the wealthy to fund public goods. His campaign emphasized working-class-centered policies [("halalflation" videos](https://substack.com/redirect/d2f6036b-87bc-4265-8ec0-35464c12ac17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) highlighting cost-of-living issues were an early signature), which resonated broadly and shifted perceptions of socialism from abstract ideology to tangible solutions.

The article notes that many DSA-elected officials, including Mamdani, operate within the Democratic Party, highlighting the group's "inside-outside" strategy: building power through grassroots organizing while running and winning Democratic primaries. This approach is contrasted with the group's small size and occasional internal tensions (e.g., debates over congressional endorsements, where Mamdani urged restraint against challenging powerful Democrats like Hakeem Jeffries to preserve coalition-building for his mayoral agenda).

The New Orleans convention setting is used symbolically and practically. The same area where a truck attack was deemed an Islamic terrorist attack that occurred on January 1, 2025. FBI Victim Services has identified at least 57 individuals who were physically injured, in addition to the 14 deceased victims, during the New Year's Day attack.

While most of the piece focuses on national implications, the location subtly underscores the DSA's ambition to expand beyond coastal strongholds like New York. References to other cities (including New Orleans itself in related reporting) show progressive policies like property tax hikes for expanded childcare gaining traction even in non-traditional left areas, suggesting Mamdani's model could inspire similar efforts nationwide.

The opinion's tone is cautiously optimistic. The author portrays DSA as at a crossroads: galvanized by Mamdani's win, but under pressure to translate electoral success into governing power and broader national influence. There's acknowledgment of challenges ahead--internal divisions, pushback from business elites and mainstream Democrats, the difficulty of scaling local wins to the federal level, and the ever-present risk of overreach or co-optation.

The piece argues that this is a pivotal moment for American socialism. Mamdani's breakthrough has "legitimized" the label and created a blueprint for winning power by addressing material needs rather than purely cultural or symbolic fights. I have some big news: I’ve recently endorsed Juliana Stratton for U.S. Senate in Illinois. We need leaders who will fight for the working people who make this country run — not the giant corporations, and not the special interests. I know Juliana will be one of those leaders in the Senate, and that’s why I’m proud to endorse her. [**If you’re able, please split a $28 donation now to support Juliana Stratton and our campaign. Your contribution will help send this fearless, progressive fighter to the Senate and strengthen our fight to make our government actually work for working people.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3461?amount=28&t=8&akid=2772%2E4032634%2EBaf0BY)

The American people are demanding change. They demand leaders who will fight for them every single day. In Illinois, Juliana is that leader. She believes in the bold solutions that this moment calls for: Medicare for All, fair taxes on the wealthy, raising the federal minimum wage, and keeping corporate PACs out of politics. She has the courage and moral clarity to take on special interests — and win. Juliana has spent her career standing up for working families, protecting reproductive freedom, and making Illinois more affordable. Now, she’s ready to take that fight to the Senate, and this is exactly the type of leadership that will strengthen the Democratic party. Donald Trump is using the presidency to enrich himself and hurt working people. But even in the face of these challenges, I believe we can make real progress — because people like Juliana are willing to fight for it. Corporate special interests are spending millions to try to stop her. The only way to fight back is to build the strongest grassroots movement behind her. If we stand together, Juliana will win — and she will fight for working people every day in the Senate. body:
Trump’s Justice Department prosecutors just tried (and failed) to indict me and five of my colleagues for stating the law in a way they didn’t like.
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2413%2E135344%2Ej0fCvd)

[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-deluzio.1N-VEN&refcode=em260213&t=2&akid=2413%2E135344%2Ej0fCvd)
---
**_BREAKING: Grand Jury Rebuffs Justice Dept. Attempt to Indict 6 Democrats in Congress_**
Friends, this is outrageous.
Trump’s Justice Department prosecutors just tried (and failed) to indict me and five of my colleagues for stating the law in a way they didn’t like. No one can force our troops to follow illegal orders, and the oath to the Constitution is sacred.
**In response? A group of regular Americans sitting on a grand jury looked at this and said: No. This is not a crime.**
That’s because Americans know and believe that our Constitution is not a polite suggestion to those in power—we take an oath to support and defend the Constitution, and that is bigger than any weak man or his even weaker enablers.
This was an abuse of power, and Americans shut it down.
**[Donald Trump and his Justice Department have tried to indict us—trying to intimidate and harass me and my colleagues. This failed attempt shows that our truth and commitment to the Constitution outweighs his threats. I will always continue to stand firm for our democracy, and I’m asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Elissa Slotkin today to help me in the fights ahead →](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-deluzio.1N-VEN&refcode=em260213&t=3&akid=2413%2E135344%2Ej0fCvd)**
Back in November, several of my colleagues and I released a video reaffirming a basic constitutional truth: the oath to the Constitution comes above all. No service member is required to follow an illegal order. Full stop.
Trump’s response? He tried to bully and intimidate us into silence.
He went so far as to have his allies at the Justice Department push for criminal charges against members of Congress for saying things he didn’t like.
**Donald Trump and his administration tried to intimidate us. Indict us.**
But a group of everyday Americans sitting on that grand jury looked at this case and shut it down.
That almost never happens. Prosecutors almost always get the indictments they ask for. The fact that American citizens rejected this tells you everything—they could see what this really was: an abuse of power meant to punish people for standing up for the Constitution.
**Friends, even in this moment of intimidation and chaos, ordinary Americans still recognize the difference between the rule of law and raw political revenge.**
I first swore an oath to the Constitution as a 17-year-old at the Naval Academy. I took that oath again when I was elected to represent Western Pennsylvania in Congress.
That oath is sacred. It’s lifelong. It doesn’t expire. And it doesn’t bend to threats or tantrums from a would-be strongman.
America isn’t about loyalty to one man, it’s about loyalty to the Constitution. Defending that is something I will never shy away from.
**[If you believe in that too, stand with me right now. Chip in to Elissa Slotkin and me to help me keep fighting for our Constitution, our democracy, and the American Dream →](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-deluzio.1N-VEN&refcode=em260213&t=4&akid=2413%2E135344%2Ej0fCvd)**

Please do not click away

**$3, Please.**
That is the contribution I am asking you to make to the New Hampshire Democratic Party.
**Please do not click away -- because this is probably one of the most strategic contributions you can make at this point in the election.**
$3 - because there is a U.S. Senate race in New Hampshire this cycle. Democrats have to win this in order to take back the Senate (and effectively end Trump's presidency), but it's going to be a very tough opponent and a close race.
$3 - because we can replace a Republican governor and both chambers of the legislature that are controlled by Republicans.
$3 - because there are TWO competitive House seats in the next election -- again, control of the House is on the line.
$3 - because Republicans in the state have threatened to redraw maps to take one of those House seats.
So ... look at how far that $3 can go -- especially when everyone is chipping-in just a few bucks. The Senate, the House, a governor's race and state legislature. And the New Hampshire Democratic Party is leading the coordinated fight on ALL OF THEM.
This is why this is such a strategic donation -- and God help us if we lose and Trump gets two more years of unchecked power.
Can I count on you?
[**Please make a $3 contribution to the New Hampshire Democratic Party today. A donation at this point in the cycle is so much more valuable than any point later. Peter, I just have to acknowledge something: It is not normal to have to be fighting so many battles on behalf of our democracy. It is not normal to have a White House ordering mid-decade congressional map redraws with the explicit purpose of gaining seats in a midterm election. And it is not normal to be waiting with great apprehension for a ruling from the highest court in the land, which will determine whether or not millions of Americans will still have the right to equal representation. None of this is normal, and none of it is easy. And that’s why I need to say thank you for sticking with this fight — for standing shoulder to shoulder with us — at this unprecedented time when so much is at stake. We're in a battle to save our democracy, and this team shows up every day with the urgency the moment demands. That matters. Most Mississippians expect Republicans to fight taxes--especially federal taxes. So it should come as no surprise that people are scratching their heads when a self-described "Republican" senator in Jackson is doing the exact opposite: asking Washington, D.C. to tax us more.
That is precisely what MS SR6 does, and it is indefensible for anyone who claims to believe in limited government, free markets, or conservative principles.
MS SR6 is not harmless. It is a formal request from Mississippi lawmakers urging Congress to impose a new federal excise tax on airguns and airbows by rolling them into the Pittman-Robertson Act. That 1937 law already taxes firearms and ammunition. Now, instead of pushing back against federal overreach, this resolution invites it--cheerleading for Washington to expand its tax authority yet again.
Let's be clear: no one in Jackson was elected to lobby for higher federal taxes.
Supporters hide behind the usual talking points: "It's for conservation" and "It's only a small tax." But Republicans are supposed to know better. Every tax starts small. Every expansion is "reasonable." And every time government reaches for a new revenue stream, it rarely lets go.
Airguns and airbows are not traditional firearms. They are affordable, low-noise, low-recoil tools used by families, young shooters, retirees, and disabled hunters. They are often the entry point into shooting sports for kids and beginners. They are also a growing area of American innovation, supported largely by small manufacturers and local retailers--not corporate giants who can easily absorb new compliance costs.
MS SR6 would make those products more expensive overnight.
Higher prices mean fewer families buying starter equipment, fewer youth programs able to participate, and fewer adaptive options for hunters who rely on air-powered alternatives. Small businesses take the hit first. Innovation slows. Choice disappears. And for what? So Mississippi politicians can help Congress find a new excuse to take more money from Mississippians' pockets?
If a Democrat proposed this, at least it would be ideologically honest. But when a Republican does it, voters are right to ask: whose side are you on?
Conservation does not require expanding federal taxation. Mississippians already support wildlife and habitat through licenses, private donations, land stewardship, and voluntary conservation groups. That approach respects freedom. A federal tax assumes government knows better than citizens how their money should be spent--and that is not a conservative principle.
Even worse, MS SR6 sets a dangerous precedent. Once lawmakers decide every new or growing product category should be taxed "for a good cause," there is no limiting principle left. Today it's airguns and airbows. Tomorrow it's something else. That is how limited government quietly dies--not with one massive tax hike, but with a series of "modest" expansions nobody was supposed to notice.
Mississippi does not need to beg Washington for more power, more money, or more control. And Republicans certainly should not be leading that charge.
If your state senator claims to be a Republican but supports MS SR6, call them out--respectfully but firmly. Tell them conservatives do not ask for new federal taxes. Tell them conservation does not require surrendering principles. And tell them Mississippi deserves representation that actually acts like it believes in limited government, not just campaigns on it.

clean_body: Mississippi Shouldn't Be Asking for More Gun Taxes | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? from the desk ofDana Criswell Mississippi Shouldn't Be Asking for More Gun Taxes | | | Feb 13 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Most Mississippians expect Republicans to fight taxes--especially federal taxes. So it should come as no surprise that people are scratching their heads when a self-described "Republican" senator in Jackson is doing the exact opposite: asking Washington, D.C. to tax us more. That is precisely what MS SR6 does, and it is indefensible for anyone who claims to believe in limited government, free markets, or conservative principles. MS SR6 is not harmless. It is a formal request from Mississippi lawmakers urging Congress to impose a new federal excise tax on airguns and airbows by rolling them into the Pittman-Robertson Act. That 1937 law already taxes firearms and ammunition. Now, instead of pushing back against federal overreach, this resolution invites it--cheerleading for Washington to expand its tax authority yet again. Let's be clear: no one in Jackson was elected to lobby for higher federal taxes. Supporters hide behind the usual talking points: "It's for conservation" and "It's only a small tax." But Republicans are supposed to know better. Every tax starts small. Every expansion is "reasonable." And every time government reaches for a new revenue stream, it rarely lets go. Airguns and airbows are not traditional firearms. They are affordable, low-noise, low-recoil tools used by families, young shooters, retirees, and disabled hunters. They are often the entry point into shooting sports for kids and beginners. They are also a growing area of American innovation, supported largely by small manufacturers and local retailers--not corporate giants who can easily absorb new compliance costs. MS SR6 would make those products more expensive overnight. Higher prices mean fewer families buying starter equipment, fewer youth programs able to participate, and fewer adaptive options for hunters who rely on air-powered alternatives. Small businesses take the hit first. Innovation slows. Choice disappears. And for what? So Mississippi politicians can help Congress find a new excuse to take more money from Mississippians' pockets? If a Democrat proposed this, at least it would be ideologically honest. But when a Republican does it, voters are right to ask: whose side are you on? Conservation does not require expanding federal taxation. Mississippians already support wildlife and habitat through licenses, private donations, land stewardship, and voluntary conservation groups. That approach respects freedom. A federal tax assumes government knows better than citizens how their money should be spent--and that is not a conservative principle. Even worse, MS SR6 sets a dangerous precedent. Once lawmakers decide every new or growing product category should be taxed "for a good cause," there is no limiting principle left. Today it's airguns and airbows. Tomorrow it's something else. That is how limited government quietly dies--not with one massive tax hike, but with a series of "modest" expansions nobody was supposed to notice. Mississippi does not need to beg Washington for more power, more money, or more control. And Republicans certainly should not be leading that charge. If your state senator claims to be a Republican but supports MS SR6, call them out--respectfully but firmly. Tell them conservatives do not ask for new federal taxes. Tell them conservation does not require surrendering principles. And tell them Mississippi deserves representation that actually acts like it believes in limited government, not just campaigns on it. Read all of Dana 's post and stay informed about politics in Mississippi | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Dana Criswell Mississippi ? ?

name: Patrick J. Murphy
subject: What My Family Taught Me About Grit, Love, and Passing It On
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/PJM_Logo.png]
It’s not every day my 80-year-old uncle ends up on the local news [https://6abc.com/post/possible-water-main-break-floods-veterans-philadelphia-home-im-ex-paratrooper-pretty-resilient/18505249/] .
Last week, a weeklong cold snap with temperatures hovering around -8 degrees caused a water main break in my Uncle Billy Rapone’s Philadelphia Fairmount neighborhood, flooding his rowhouse basement with three feet of water and cutting off heat to the block.
When the ABC news crew arrived asking neighbors how they were holding up, they met a 5’7” Vietnam combat paratrooper who still does push-ups on his living room floor.
The reporter asked: “How are you going to get by without heat?”
Billy looked her dead in the eye, still wearing his Vietnam Airborne Vet baseball cap, and said: “I survived Vietnam as an Airborne Paratrooper. This ain’t nothing.”
That’s the kind of person my Uncle Billy is.
And he’s the reason I became Airborne.
I wrote about him and his impact on me in my latest for Substack [https://open.substack.com/pub/patrickmurphypa/p/my-uncle-survived-vietnam-a-frozen?r=14qjx&utm_medium=ios&shareImageVariant=overlay] .
He wasn’t the only family member who shaped me, though.
It began with my grandparents.
They never talked about leadership or framed their lives around legacy or influence. What they modeled instead was something simpler and more durable: responsibility without performance, faith without spectacle, and a steady commitment to the people in front of them. You showed up, carried your weight, and didn't make hardship louder than it needed to be.
That posture became the undertone of everything that followed. As their children grew, served, struggled, married, and built lives of their own, those same expectations carried forward—not identically, but recognizably.
Different personalities, different paths, but the same orientation toward work, family, faith and service. Over time, those examples multiplied almost imperceptibly.
I didn't grow up thinking of it as anything cohesive. Only later did I realize that what shaped me wasn't one person or one moment, but accumulation—a density of living examples. A network of people whose lives overlapped with mine long enough to matter.
I didn't grow up in a house with 27 people under one roof, but I might as well have. We were close enough that their lives overlapped with mine in ways that mattered. Sunday dinners for all 27 were made by my Grandmom Kay Rapone. We were close enough that I watched how they handled stress, failure, responsibility, and love.
Over time, I took to heart something different from each of them.
There was Uncle Joe, a Korean War era 11th Airborne paratrooper who came home and rose through the ranks of the Philadelphia Police Department, making it all the way up to Inspector. My mom—Billy’s twin sister—who was a star student and later entered religious life, modeling discipline, faith, and service in a completely different way. My dad, steady and reliable, taught me what it means to be present day after day.
We’d leave at 5am for hockey practices every weekend and he’d look forward to the vending machine coffee at the old rink, while my brother and I rose through the ranks and eventually both captained our hockey teams in college.
My brother JJ, who taught me loyalty, humor, and the importance of having someone who always has your back.
My sister Cathy, fiercely loyal who always led with her heart, a model and then Penn State cheerleader, we had to bite our lips at the annoyingly ‘affectionate’ comments from our classmates.
Aunts, uncles, cousins—each one carrying themselves a little differently, each one leaving an imprint.
When I joined the Army, it felt less like a dramatic decision and more like a natural next step. My dad and three uncles (two who served in Vietnam) took me under their wing, but none more than Uncle Billy. On my enlistment form, when they asked what I wanted to do, I wrote: "I want to be an Airborne Ranger with the 82nd Airborne Division."
I was following a path I had already seen walked.
Today, the 27 Murphys are my core family as it exists now—we vacation every summer together, where the broader family meets for ‘Cousins Club’ in my cousin Tony’s North Wildwood house - the people whose lives intersect daily, whose emotional temperature I help set, whose sense of safety, stability, and direction is shaped in part by how I show up.
As a son , leadership looks like honoring what was given. Carrying forward sacrifice without romanticizing it. Staying grounded in gratitude and responsibility rather than entitlement. Watching Eagles games on the couch instead of at the actual game so we can enjoy it together, and I can help take the edge off his disappointment when they don’t win.
As a brother , leadership means showing up, telling the truth, and not vanishing when things get hard. Being the uncle to his five girls and knowing me and their cousins are always a phone call or text away.
As an uncle , I've learned that the younger people in your life are always paying attention, even when you think they're not. They notice what you let slide, what makes you laugh, what you choose to address and what you ignore. How actions always speak louder than words.
As a friend , leadership is trust built over time. That means listening more than talking. Keeping confidence. And being present without needing to be center of attention.
As an advocate , leadership means standing up when it matters and creating space for others because with power comes great responsibility, especially when no one is watching.
And as a father to Jack and Maggie, leadership is no longer theoretical at all.
It’s fully lived.
It’s how I handle stress when things don’t go according to plan.
How I speak about other people when my kids are listening and watching what I share on social media.
How I respond to disappointment with grace and grit, happening more often than those on the outside will ever know.
Whether strength shows up as calm or as volatility. They’ve seen both sides of me as their protector and patriot.
I want my kids to understand that strength doesn’t always have to be loud. But there are times it needs to be and they have to be ready.
I tell them about Uncle Billy’s military career more than my own, but I also tell them the rest of his story: how he struggled in school, earned his GED, followed his brother into the Army, and found confidence and purpose through service.
When I saw Uncle Billy on the news, I understood something clearly. That moment didn’t begin with him. It began generations earlier—and now it runs through our generation.
- Patrick
Be sure to follow me on Instagram [https://www.instagram.com/patrickmurphypa/?hl=en] and subscribe to my Substack [https://substack.com/@patrickmurphypa] for my weekly geopolitical and business analysis .

| | | | | [](https://e96gjzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001kZHiVeheT32MbBF_JFkM0GwjLcotSQBiwhzdbFUGd4cTvby3-iqJ72wrQl9szmaypjW8qxBH8IoTZCO6QMhYtW8UWNCgMKMamq6vAxG3EonBdcWV5xK9s1Cb8CB2GjOfe_LowjNOaYeHHPkJn5bnGVum062-i6tqWdfOgT8kAqPFxz9_dsDOXdFrCY0S9lr87whzfjuyydWr1eFaj9jJqsb388NgpcMq3O_Ne0L3p5E=&c=0ygYUU58Vo5FcocYNKtMPTq3hWUu3hvMStGHXJLuwhFAzFHjwxA7Ug==&ch=UMT9EdaALE6RJoAEbX0vrwX2cDCjtKyQEW17wkCdXPhsj4JVtyRz8g==)

|
Peter,
Right now, the United States spends $850 billion every year on the military-- while our kids' schools are left scrambling for resources. As Trump slashes education funding and pushes to dismantle the Department of Education, states are being forced to hike property taxes just to fill the gap.
Here in Illinois, we have the highest property taxes in the country -- and still, only 1 in 4 fourth graders are meeting reading standards. In wealthier zip codes, students see far better results, while kids in working-class and low-income communities are left behind. A child's zip code shouldn't determine whether they get a good education. But right now, it does.
That's why when I get to Congress, I'll introduce the Books Not Bombs Act.
---
| | [](https://e96gjzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001kZHiVeheT32MbBF_JFkM0GwjLcotSQBiwhzdbFUGd4cTvby3-iqJ72wrQl9szmaypjW8qxBH8IoTZCO6QMhYtW8UWNCgMKMamq6vAxG3EonBdcWV5xK9s1Cb8CB2GjOfe_LowjNOaYeHHPkJn5bnGVum062-i6tqWdfOgT8kAqPFxz9_dsDOXdFrCY0S9lr87whzfjuyydWr1eFaj9jJqq1_j67XZGJYOF3SzE3x-rU=&c=0ygYUU58Vo5FcocYNKtMPTq3hWUu3hvMStGHXJLuwhFAzFHjwxA7Ug==&ch=UMT9EdaALE6RJoAEbX0vrwX2cDCjtKyQEW17wkCdXPhsj4JVtyRz8g==)

|
This bill will shift just 1.5% of the Pentagon's budget into public education. That small reallocation would mean a 10% increase in funding for our schools -- enough to ensure every child gets the education they deserve while driving down property taxes and making housing more affordable for homeowners and renters alike.
This is how we tackle the root causes of poor public education while making life more affordable for working people. This is why Congress needs more school board members in the fight -- people like me, who have seen firsthand how broken our system is and who know how to fix it.
[But I can't do it without you. This campaign is powered by grassroots supporters -- not billionaires, not defense contractors. The bill aims to prevent noncitizens from voting in federal elections and would require information-sharing between state election officials and federal authorities to verify citizenship on voter rolls. ---
Peter,
After Democrats started striking back in the redistricting wars, Trump realized something: his election-rigging scheme isn't working. It's backfiring. Bigly.
So now MAGA is scrambling in Utah to try to overturn Proposition 4, the anti-gerrymandering reform Utah voters passed in 2018. If they succeed, Republicans could wipe out another Democratic seat in Congress with the stroke of a pen.
But their effort is collapsing in the most MAGA way.
They have until February 15 to submit enough signatures to get their repeal on the ballot -- and they're tens of thousands short.
But it gets worse.

| | | Hi, DSCC Vice Chair Mark Kelly here. I want to talk to you about a _key_ opportunity in front of us as we fight for the Senate majority: **special elections.**

I know a thing or two about these kinds of races, because I got to the Senate by _winning_ a special election back in 2020 — even as Republicans spent over $70 million to stop me. **And my victory proved mission-critical, because without it, Democrats wouldn't have had a Senate majority.**

[**Now, history could repeat itself. Two special elections coming up in Ohio and Florida are among a small handful of races that could decide the majority — again. So I'm coming to ask you, will you donate $5 to win races like those and take back the Senate? >>**](https://go.dscc.org/go/22350?amount=5&t=5&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=5&amounts=5%2C10%2C20%2C50&code=DPE-FD-20260213-MarkKelly-KellySpecialElectionsFR-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20260213-MarkKelly-KellySpecialElectionsFR-Pros-sl1&akid=22719%2E9716520%2E1Y3XS2)

I want to be clear, team: **These special elections give us an opportunity we would have waited YEARS for without them, and they make a BIG difference.**

In fact, during Donald Trump's first term, Democrats flipped **_three_** Senate seats in special elections, including mine, my good friend Raphael Warnock's, and even a seat in dark-red Alabama. Each time, we defeated Trump-endorsed candidates who would have been guaranteed votes for his destructive agenda, and instead we elected Democrats who fought for hardworking Americans.

**Now, we're facing the same task again — but it won't be easy.** Trump is reportedly "obsessed" with the midterms, National Republicans will spend big-time to keep their majority, and just like when I first won, Democrats only need to flip a handful of seats to take back the Senate.

**Take it from someone who's been in this position before: We'll need your help to make the most of this opportunity — and that's why I'm reaching out.**

**[As a DSCC Vice Chair, I'm personally asking: Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can to help Democrats win in states like Ohio and Florida and take back the Senate? Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Fox 7 Austin: New Postal Service guidance on postmarks could affect ballot, tax deadlines [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=021326_1&amount=25]
The day you mail something may no longer count as the actual mailing date, Team.
Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office.
USPS has now reversed that practice. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility, not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over.
What does this mean? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control.
Our first priority is making sure every voter understands this change and how it can impact them -- not just in terms of vote-by-mail, but their bills, their taxes, responses to companies, you name it. What we all think is the deadline may not be the deadline and that's a huge deal that's being under-reported by the media.
We also need to make sure every mail-in voter across the country knows how to get their ballot in on time, especially those most vulnerable to this change, like the elderly, rural Americans who live far from USPS regional facilities, our military service members, and young people who are voting by mail away from home.
Team, will you pitch in $35 or whatever you can today and help us spread the word about these changes so we can protect mail-in ballots? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=021326_1&amount=35]

name: Roy Cooper
subject: My mom was a teacher.
body:
This is why it’s so important to me.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/2365?source=&t=1&akid=564%2E124072%2E6HMPhn)
_I’d like to tell you about someone important to me, Peter._ My mom, Beverly Cooper, passed away in 2013 after a long, wonderful life, but her memory continues to inspire me daily. Mom spent decades teaching in public schools in Nash County, where I grew up and where my daughters and I went to public schools. [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5445?t=7&akid=564%2E124072%2E6HMPhn) _Beverly Cooper (right) at Roy and Kristin’s wedding._ **The dedication my mom gave to her students every day — nights, weekends, and summers included — showed me firsthand the lengths our public school teachers go to give children the best possible start.** As the son of a teacher and a graduate of public schools, I grew up with a deep appreciation for educators and knowing the value of a quality public school education. It’s why advocating for public education has been a priority of mine during my entire career in public service. As Governor, I worked hard to get raises for public school teachers. Across America, too many teachers find they have to work second and third jobs just to make ends meet. Teachers can’t give their best in the classroom if they’re worried about putting food on the table at home, and if we want to hire the best teachers, we need to pay them like the professionals they are. We also invested more than a billion dollars in early childhood learning and care to set our youngest learners up for success throughout their education. Peter, these are the kinds of ambitious investments we need to be making on a national scale. Schools and teachers everywhere in NC and this country deserve the resources they need so each student can get an excellent education that will prepare them for college, a career, or whatever comes next. **Unfortunately, right-wing Republicans in Raleigh and Washington have made it clear that they’d rather take resources away from education than invest in the success of future generations. They attack the teachers who devote themselves to their profession in order to stoke fear and win political campaigns.** _Students and teachers deserve better. They deserve elected leaders who are on their side._ Peter, I remain committed to the fight for public education. _It’s just what’s right._ **[If you can afford a small donation today to help me take this fight to Washington, it would go a long way. My opponents have the GOP mega-donor machine lined up to spend _hundreds of millions_ against me, and I can’t take them on alone.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5445?t=8&akid=564%2E124072%2E6HMPhn)** | **[DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5445?t=9&akid=564%2E124072%2E6HMPhn)**

body:
We know what you’re thinking.
#

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/63703?c0=giffords-em-q12026.1ZloXK&refcode=em250213-1-b&t=1&akid=11251%2E3935704%2ERPKzMK)
Team,
With just 48 hours until our first mid-quarter deadline of the election year, Gabby Giffords is asking you to donate $1 to help GIFFORDS PAC end gun violence in America.
Yes, just $1.
We know what you’re thinking...“how can $1 make an impact?”
$1 might not mean a lot on its own — but by the time you read this, a few people have already taken the step to donate that $1.
They’ve seen the devastating headlines about preventable gun violence across the country. They also know the power of this collective team, and they’re hoping you join them to help save more lives.
Suddenly, that $1 gift adds up to $10,000 or even $25,000 of impact. We then have the resources to run more ads and reach voters in the most competitive of races.
_And look, persuading even a few hundred more voters to go to the polls could mean the difference between winning and losing._
If even a quarter of the people reading this email donated $1, we would reach our ambitious fundraising goal and could use that money to stand up against the gun lobby’s spending. But not everyone can, which is why we are asking you:
[**Will you contribute $1 — or more, if you’re feeling generous — so GIFFORDS PAC can reach our fundraising goal before our deadline tomorrow night?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/63703?c0=giffords-em-q12026.1ZloXK&refcode=em250213-1-b&t=2&akid=11251%2E3935704%2ERPKzMK)

Masked federal agents are stationed in cities across the nation. Dissent is being stifled by fear and intimidation. The rule of law is being ignored — _and even attacked_ — by Trump and his closest enablers.
It can feel hopeless and we can be tempted to give in to despair.

Beto

body:
I’m not going to speak in platitudes or shy away from what I believe. There is a war going on in this country, and the oligarchy and the fascists are winning right now.

Peter,
Nothing pisses me off more than getting a fundraising text from Democrats talking about how they’re fighting fascism... Because it’s such B.S. We’re not idiots. Everyone knows most of them aren’t doing jack right now to fight back.
People are being kidnapped into unmarked vans by masked police. There is a genocide happening in Palestine. Literal billionaires have taken over our government. And all Democratic leadership can do is send us another fundraising text?
**My name is Graham Platner, and I’m the Marine Corps veteran and Democrat running for U.S. Senate against Susan Collins here in Maine.** I’m not going to speak in platitudes or shy away from what I believe. There is a war going on in this country, and the oligarchy and the fascists are winning right now.
**Susan Collins is the most vulnerable Republican senator in the country.** We have an opportunity to replace her with a working-class Democrat – one who won’t take money from corporations or AIPAC.
But I’m not a wealthy guy, and we’re still short of our $50,000 goal and what we need to win. **If I’m going to be able to defeat Susan Collins and flip this Senate seat blue, I need folks like you to chip in now to our campaign.**
**[Please, will you split a donation right now between our campaign and Heartland Patriots to help me defeat Susan Collins, flip Maine blue, and take back the Senate with a Democrat who will actually fight to defend our democracy like Democrats oughta be?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/100584?refcode=em20260213-10054&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10054%2E614464%2E8K5KyJ)**
In the history of this nation, power has never been just willingly handed to the people. Another mealy-mouthed Democrat isn’t going to fix things or protect our constitution.
I’m ready to go to the United States Senate and fight – but I need your help today to get there.
In solidarity,
Graham Platner

clean_body: | | | | Dear Friend, This week marked a major milestone for the State Freedom Caucus Network and a reminder of why this movement matters.With the launch of the West Virginia Freedom Caucus , our network now spans 14 states. In one of the most conservative states in the country, lawmakers are organizing to ensure that Republican supermajorities actually govern like conservatives.Here’s what happened and why it matters. | WEST VIRGINIA The West Virginia Freedom Caucus officially launched this week, exclusively reported by West Virginia is overwhelmingly Republican:President Trump won the state with nearly 70% of the vote , compared to Kamala Harris’s 28%. The legislature looks similar:State House: 91 Republicans, 9 DemocratsState Senate: 32 Republicans, 2 DemocratsOn paper, that should look like Florida — a beacon of conservative reform. But it hasn’t. As we see in too many red states, lawmakers campaign as Republicans and govern like Democrats once in office. The West Virginia Freedom Caucus is organizing to change that dynamic. As WVFC Chairman explained, the caucus will focus on eliminating “as many taxes as possible” and reducing the “size and scope of government” so West Virginians can actually take care of themselves. And they will challenge not just Democrats, but the liberal Republicans who try to stop them. With a new conservative governor, Patrick Morrissey, in office, disciplined legislators committed to real reform will help ensure conservative promises translate into conservative policy.BOTTOM LINE: Red states should govern red. The West Virginia Freedom Caucus now exists to make sure that happens. | SOUTH CAROLINA South Carolina has long been labeled a “Judicial Hellhole,” ranking #3 nationally in . The problem? Lawmakers — many of whom are trial lawyers — help select and confirm judges, then argue cases in front of those same judges. The conflict of interest is obvious. This week, with strong support from the South Carolina Freedom Caucus - and by SCFC member, Rep. Joe White — judicial reform legislation advanced across the finish line in the State House. The bill restructures the Judicial Merit Selection Commission and removes lawmakers’ direct control over judicial selection.Why did trial lawyers masquerading as state lawmakers pass a bill in the house that would negatively affect their own scheme? Because the SC Freedom Caucus, House Freedom Caucus member Ralph Norman (who's running for governor), and a huge grassroots army forced them to do it. The bill now faces an uphill battle in the State Senate, but the pressure will remain high for the upper chamber to pass it. When insiders control the bench, reform is overdue.BOTTOM LINE: As Ronald Reagan said, "If you want them to see the light, make them feel the heat." That motto is standard operating procedure for your State Freedom Caucuses. | QUICK HITS 👉 Wyoming: An “anti-grooming” bill backed by the Wyoming Freedom Caucus survived by just one vote — 43–19 — because 13 liberal Republicans joined all 6 Democrats to oppose it. During a budget session, a 42-vote supermajority was required. The vote went national after Libs of TikTok on social media and Elon Musk commented, generating over 1.6 million views. What used to be quiet votes are now exposed for the whole world to see thanks to the WY Freedom Caucus. 👉 Election Integrity: The U.S. House the SAVE America Act to strengthen voter ID requirements and prevent non-citizens from voting with full support from House Freedom Caucus members. In the same week, the Arizona Freedom Caucus similar election integrity legislation through the State House. 👉 Louisiana: Louisiana Freedom Caucus member Rep. Danny McCormick legislation allowing people to carry firearms on college campuses, arguing that “gun free zones don’t stop evil — armed citizens do.” Republicans hold supermajorities in both chambers. So if this bill fails, it won’t be because of the Democrats. 👉 National Spotlight: I joined the popular TimCast News podcast how the “50 Swamps” in our state capitols are often more corrupt than Washington, D.C. — as hard as that may be to believe. | HELP US HOLD THE LINE The launch of the West Virginia Freedom Caucus is proof that this movement is growing — state by state.But growth doesn’t happen automatically. It requires organization, resources, and a willingness to confront entrenched power wherever it hides.If you believe conservative states should actually govern conservatively, we need your support. We'll be back with another update soon. Until then, please be sure to our efforts so that we can support our State Freedom Caucuses!In Liberty, Andy RothPresident State Freedom Caucus Network | |

name: Kirk Cameron
subject: Fight Back Against Hollywoodâ€™sAgenda with Iggy and Mr. Kirk
body:
Today you have a very special chance to stop the Hollywood groomers who are turning our children and grandchildren against us and the Godly values we love.

| | | You are absolutely right if you think Hollywood is reaching right into your family living room with "entertainment" that grooms children.
---
| |
---
| | Dear Friend in Faith,Please – for the sake of all our families – take it from me as someone who’s lived and worked in Hollywood my whole life... You are absolutely right if you think Hollywood is reaching right into your family living room with “entertainment” that grooms children.You may remember shows with wholesome messages like Father Knows Best, Marcus Welby, M.D., and even Dennis the Menace.But today when children turn on the TV, they see a Drag Queen leading the Pride Parade on _Blue’s Clues_...
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zs1t9ejdbhd0tgqifd8nk6d8a35h188chekmeuig_rp22sh2s8i6epr4c1i69p34c3h2bs)
---
| | Or Sesame Street using YOUR tax-dollars to normalize same-sex parents and men in dresses.And the result is an upside-down world where children lecture YOU about what you can and cannot say... ...and they try to “educate” YOU about your “old-fashioned” and “mean” ideas.Today you have a very special chance to stop the Hollywood groomers who are turning our children and grandchildren against us and the Godly values we love. **[Today, I’m inviting you to be a Founding Supporter of the very first children’s television show that actively fights back against the groomers in Hollywood AND reinforces the traditional biblical values that made America great.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2za32bj66gds4lr32beq4tpooeckrtlsvsp6t21uo_rp22sh2s8i6epr4c1i69p34c3h2bs)** Introducing: _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_.I’m making this ground-breaking live-action television show with the great folks at **Brave Books**.If you’ve seen me and **Brave Books** on _Fox News_ , you know we’ve already countered those awful “Drag Queen Story Hours” the Left has been pushing on children in our taxpayer funded libraries. Thanks to support from parents, grandparents, and concerned citizens just like you, we started hosting Godly and patriotic “Story Hours” of our own.And now, THOUSANDS of children and parents can gather to pledge allegiance to our flag, read wholesome books, and pray together in their libraries.It’s encouraging to see we can win when we fight back! Now we’re working to have that same impact in television.
---
>> Imagine a children's show that leaves your child or grandchild with a greater sense of right and wrong and an understanding of truth.Courage, honesty, discernment, forgiveness, empathy, all taught through a biblical and traditional lens. >> Imagine a children's show that brings families together instead of driving them apart.>> Now imagine YOU are the one who makes that show possible. Because we can’t beat the Hollywood groomers without your help as a **Founding Supporter**.
---
The great news is that we’ve already completed and released the first ten character-building episodes of _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_! We premiered it recently to a small group of children and parents and I wish you could have seen the smiles on those innocent little faces.And I wish you could have experienced _the parents_ watching their children absorb the beautiful Gospel messages.It was quite a moment for everyone – including folks just like you – who worked so hard to get us that far. But now **Brave Books** has an urgent two-fold problem that I hope you can help with.
---
_**#1. Brave Books needs to launch a massive advertising blitz to get around the groomers on the Left.**_
---
You see, we’ve made the first five episodes of Season 1 of _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ available absolutely FREE. That’s the best way we can reach MILLIONS of families with our Gospel-inspired messaging.But no one will see it if we can’t get the word out. And the Left will try to bury _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ at every turn. The price tag for an advertising blitz of this magnitude is $250,000 – and with the recent launch, we need to raise the funds immediately.
---
_**#2. We must complete Season 2 to keep our momentum going and that cost is $250,000 for post production.**_
---
I know that’s a lot of money but it’s actually a fraction of what it would cost if we made our show with a major Hollywood studio. And obviously, we won’t work through Hollywood.Hollywood has done quite enough already to destroy American culture and hijack our children.We parents, grandparents, and concerned citizens must take over to rebuild a thriving, healthy, GOOD and GODLY culture. **[That’s why I’m asking you to please contribute $35, $50, $250, $500, $2,500 or more to help us reach our fundraising goal of $250,000 for advertising and $250,000 for Season 2.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zhfaiit3bklmul82mimruqf18gqtjfpomjh9c61g_rp22sh2s8i6epr4c1i69p34c3h2bs) ** As our special “Thank You” for becoming a **Founding Supporter** at the $50 level, we’ll send you all ten episodes of Season 1 of _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ FREE on DVD.This exclusive _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ DVD is only offered to **Founding Supporters**. It won’t be available for sale anywhere. So with **[**your gift of $50**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zg7tqd8d5a7an8hhsjobo9g60jqko7euro69fl10_rp22sh2s8i6epr4c1i69p34c3h2bs)** , you’ll be part of a small select group of people who own our wholesome TV show on DVD. You’ll have it ready to watch with the children in your life. Or you can drop your DVD by your local school, church, mission, or even leave it in the waiting room at your doctor’s office. So many children have no way of hearing God’s message in their lives. Your random act of kindness may change a child’s life. **[So please – whether you can send $50, $5,000, $25,000, or anything higher or lower, please respond quickly and know that gifts of EVERY size are needed and greatly appreciated.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z7eh6k45k7iuqu1cvlf095cdf9pgn9567u7602qg_rp22sh2s8i6epr4c1i69p34c3h2bs)** There’s no time to waste. Hollywood groomers have destroyed America’s Godly culture. But today we rebuild from the ashes.And it starts by ensuring the most innocent among us are filled with faith and family – not filth.Thank you for being a part of history by becoming a **Founding Supporter** of _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_.
---
Sincerely,
---
| | Kirk Cameron (and Iggy!)Actor, Author, and Father

---
**Kirk Cameron (and Iggy!)** **Actor, Author, and Father**
---
|
---
| | P.S. The #1 thing you can do today to stop the Hollywood groomers who are tearing families apart – maybe even yours – is to support the very first children’s television show in _history_ made possible by contributions from grandparents and seniors like you. **[Please send in your Founding Supporter gift and help me reclaim America with the Biblical values our country was founded upon.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zj58p9l38t61cbculpak4mcl2pcljie240h6uu58_rp22sh2s8i6epr4c1i69p34c3h2bs)** Thank you and God bless you and your family! -- Kirk

### First came our momentum, then came the MAGA dark money
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Feb 13
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..FKx7MwCcfc0DdJlNt9mDExwtRXHG2fSsg2ujqsBlgVQ?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/they-noticed?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

It's almost a sure thing:
The leaves turn in Northern Michigan every fall. The Tigers take the field every spring. And in politics, when a grassroots campaign starts gaining momentum, the GOP dark money comes pouring in.
The most predictable thing in politics just happened to us. Here's the short version:
1️⃣ First, we outraised Mike Rogers.
2️⃣ Then, MAGA dark money dropped $500,000 into this race.
3️⃣ Now? We fight back. Together.
**I want to be honest with you: I don 't have billionaire friends.**
Unlike Mike Rogers, I don't have a MAGA Texas Big Oil megadonor backing my campaign. But I have something better -- _you._
And when everyday people like you stand up and demand a government that actually works for working families, that's when we put the MAGA super PACs on their heels. That's exactly what happened here in Michigan.
**Almost immediately after our fourth-quarter fundraising numbers went public last week, Republican dark-money groups announced they were pouring hundreds of thousands of dollars into this battleground race.** Their first ads backing Mike Rogers are about to roll out.
That's not a coincidence. It's a reminder of how this works. They're trying to drown us out.
I don't share this to be alarmist. I share it because what you're seeing right now is the contrast in this race coming into focus.
On one side, you have GOP dark-money groups who don't really know or care about Michigan.
On the other side, you have our campaign - built by teachers and nurses, autoworkers and small business owners, retirees and students. People who care deeply about this state and are willing to come together to fight for a better future.
That's the difference. We've talked about it before, but it's not abstract anymore.
Everyone knows Michigan is one of the most competitive Senate races in the country. The polls show Mike Rogers and me tied, and control of the U.S. Senate will very likely come down to this battleground race.
Now that it's clear to these MAGA medadonors that this campaign means business - that the stakes have gotten higher.
Outside money is going to keep coming, and the only way to meet this moment is to keep doing exactly what we've been doing - standing together.
So today, I'm asking you to do what this team already knows how to do: show up, pitch in if you can, and keep believing that people-powered campaigns still matter.
**If you 're in a position to chip in $10 or $20 and help us respond to these dark-money attacks, I'd be so grateful. Every contribution -- even a few dollars -- helps us make sure Michigan voters, not out-of-state billionaires, decide this race.**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/019a7507-a219-46d0-8447-fb6c9d4e9f2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And if you're not able to give right now, please know this: I've still got your back. I'll fight for you either way. This campaign is stronger because you're here.
Let's stick together.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/019a7507-a219-46d0-8447-fb6c9d4e9f2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

People who care deeply about this state and are willing to come together to fight for a better future. That's the difference. We've talked about it before, but it's not abstract anymore. Everyone knows Michigan is one of the most competitive Senate races in the country. The polls show Mike Rogers and me tied, and control of the U.S. Senate will very likely come down to this battleground race. Now that it's clear to these MAGA medadonors that this campaign means business - that the stakes have gotten higher. Outside money is going to keep coming, and the only way to meet this moment is to keep doing exactly what we've been doing - standing together. So today, I'm asking you to do what this team already knows how to do: show up, pitch in if you can, and keep believing that people-powered campaigns still matter. If you 're in a position to chip in $10 or $20 and help us respond to these dark-money attacks, I'd be so grateful. Every contribution -- even a few dollars -- helps us make sure Michigan voters, not out-of-state billionaires, decide this race. And if you're not able to give right now, please know this: I've still got your back. I'll fight for you either way. This campaign is stronger because you're here. Let's stick together. With grit and gratitude, Haley * A personal note from Haley 👋 I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love. But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican. I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win. If you're with me, will you chip in today? Paid for by Haley Stevens for Senate. | | | (C) 2026 Haley for MI 33717 Woodward Ave #539, Birmingham, MI 48009 ? ?

name: Joe Hamill
subject: Why we choose the hard fights
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Way to Lead PAC
body:
Others chase the loudest or the safest fights, but that’s not how progress happens |
---
Peter, Some people think progress happens when you chase the loudest fights or the safest ones. **We don’t.** At Way to Lead PAC, we believe winning is a discipline — something you build with intention, judgment, and a willingness to take on hard fights that actually move the needle. Since 2018, we’ve focused on races others overlook. Close margins. Down-ballot contests. Primaries where the outcome shapes power for a decade, not a news cycle. We invest where the stakes are real, and the path to victory is narrow — because that’s where durable power is built. **That approach works.** With it, Way to Lead has helped elect fighters around the country — including names you might recognize, like Raphael Warnock, Greg Casar, Summer Lee, and Maxwell Frost — and names you might not, like Ana Hernandez in Phoenix, Molly Cook in Houston, and Nabila Parks in Georgia. In 2024, Way to Lead won 55% of our races at the same time Democrats suffered nationwide losses. We helped direct millions of dollars into strategic interventions in some of the closest races in the country. We backed candidates who ran where Republicans had grown comfortable and complacent. In many cases, we faced massive spending disadvantages — and we still won. We helped eliminate Republican state supermajorities, protect razor-thin margins, and flip seats that determined who holds power over utility rates and other local policies today. We don’t pick candidates just because they poll well or make good Instagram videos. We endorse them because they reflect the communities they serve — and because with the right strategy, the right support, and the right long-term vision behind them, their victory will bring real change for real working people. That means investing beyond election night. Building infrastructure that lasts. Supporting leaders even when the road is steep. And understanding that representation without power doesn’t hold — but power, built carefully, does. **This is how maps change. Not all at once. But where it counts.** **[If you believe in choosing smart battles that can change the political map, add your name. Stand with us in the tough fights that build lasting power.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125325784/601422322/-1195751224?refcode=AU_WTL_EG_WEL_PET_NTL_202602_AM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNS8xLzkxMTI4IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImFkZTQxNjkyLWZmMDgtZjExMS04MzJlLTAwMjI0ODJhOTczMyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=UIbJqi-R4Ia4EDl2Ulvar2QokGVm0_hleGkWbGJ1E0o=&emci=f6d4ab1a-3708-f111-832e-0022482a9733&emdi=ade41692-ff08-f111-832e-0022482a9733&ceid=5054002)** | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125325786/601422325/-1195751224?refcode=AU_WTL_EG_WEL_PET_NTL_202602_AM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNS8xLzkxMTI4IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImFkZTQxNjkyLWZmMDgtZjExMS04MzJlLTAwMjI0ODJhOTczMyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=UIbJqi-R4Ia4EDl2Ulvar2QokGVm0_hleGkWbGJ1E0o=&emci=f6d4ab1a-3708-f111-832e-0022482a9733&emdi=ade41692-ff08-f111-832e-0022482a9733&ceid=5054002)

subject: Stand with Tom Willis to Protect WV & The Border
body:
West Virginia deserves a fighter, not a career politician.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/a25cb0c2072f/stand-with-tom-willis-to-protect-wv-the-border?e=a0285cc040)

# Stand with Tom Willis to Protect
# West Virginia and Our Borders
---
|
---
|
---
| | Dear Friend,
West Virginia deserves a fighter, not a career politician. I’m Tom Willis, a Christian husband, father, small business owner, State Senator, and 25-year Special Forces Green Beret. I’ve served our country at home and abroad, defending the freedoms important to our republic.
Today, our nation faces a growing threat at our borders. Illegal immigration puts West Virginians at risk and strains local resources. Law enforcement, including ICE, plays a critical role in protecting communities, enforcing our laws, and keeping families safe. Strong borders are essential to national security, public safety, and preserving our way of life.
As your U.S. Senator, I will fight to secure our borders, support law enforcement, and defend West Virginia families. I’ll ensure our government prioritizes Americans first over special interests, enforces our laws fairly, and stops the dangerous surge of illegal immigration that threatens our communities.
Your support is crucial. Stand with me in the fight to protect West Virginia values, our families, and our future.
**Vote Tom Willis in the May 12 Republican Primary.**
Thank you for standing strong for West Virginia.
Sincerely,
**Tom Willis**

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
