Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. Team — Arizona Republicans just elected a new state party chairman. His name is Sergio Arellano, and he says the most important issue facing Arizona is "the alarmingly radical Democratic Party." Some Senate Democrats love to talk a big game. “We’ll stand up to Trump.
We’ll stop authoritarianism. We’ll defend our democracy.”

But when it comes to Trump’s judicial nominees — the ones he handpicked to
sit on lifetime seats — they fold. Over and over.

These judges refuse to admit the 2020 election was legitimate. They refuse
to call January 6th an insurrection. They dodge questions, stonewall, and
give vague, meaningless answers.

And yet... 19 Senate Democrats keep advancing them.

We’ve seen it over and over: Senate Democrats talk, they posture, they
claim they’re “resisting” Trump — but when it comes to action or actually
defending our democracy, they roll over and let Trump’s cronies slide
right onto the federal bench.

Hi Peter, I’m Carina -- Randy’s wife. Randy and I just celebrated our 14th anniversary, from high school sweethearts to building a life rooted in love, faith, and the same community that raised us. When I think about that number, I feel it in my heart. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125329619/601432611/949478007?refcode=em-2.13.26-all-b&amount=14&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2I5NDk0MjQtMDYwOS1mMTExLTgzMmUtMDAyMjQ4MmE5NzMzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=HgW6C-zWANmziGL3MTCAcIaqNDIIPEJvp_Q9R5XgXAU=) Fourteen years ago, we were just two kids with big dreams and no roadmap - only love, grit, and a deep belief in where we come from. Since then, we’ve built a life through sacrifice, through long nights and early mornings, through moments that stretched us and moments that strengthened us. We’ve faced hard seasons that could have broken us - but instead, they built us. And through it all, one thing has never changed: Randy’s heart for our community. I’ve watched him pour himself into others the same way he pours himself into our family. I’ve seen the fire in his eyes when he talks about the Central Valley - about the families working two jobs, about the kids who deserve better schools, about the parents who just want a fair shot. This campaign isn’t politics to us. It’s personal. It’s about love in action. Tomorrow is Valentine's Day, and as we celebrate 14 years together, we’re asking you to channel that same love into something bigger. **[Will you make a contribution of $14 in honor of our anniversary?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125329620/601432612/949478007?refcode=em-2.13.26-all-b&amount=14&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2I5NDk0MjQtMDYwOS1mMTExLTgzMmUtMDAyMjQ4MmE5NzMzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=HgW6C-zWANmziGL3MTCAcIaqNDIIPEJvp_Q9R5XgXAU=)** Fourteen dollars. One dollar for every year we’ve chosen each other. One dollar for every year we’ve believed that ordinary people deserve extraordinary representation. Your $14 isn’t just a donation. It’s fuel. It’s hope. It’s a declaration that love is louder than doubt - and that this community is worth fighting for. Let’s show Randy that the love he gives so freely is being met with a movement that believes just as fiercely. **This bill proposes a Mississippi constitutional amendment to let voters propose, amend, or repeal state statutes by citizen initiative and approve or reject them at the ballot, subject to procedural and subject-matter limits.**
### Bill basics
* **Vehicle:** Senate Concurrent Resolution (constitutional amendment)
* **Election date:** **November 2026** general election
* **Committees/Referral:** Elections
* **What it changes:** Amends **Sections 33, 56, 61, and 72** of the MS Constitution to create an initiative process for **statutes** (not constitutional provisions).

### Key provisions
* **Creates initiative power for statutes:** People can propose new laws or amend/repeal existing laws by petition and election, independent of the Legislature.
* **Limits what initiatives can do:** No initiatives for:
* Constitutional amendments (must go through the constitutional process)
* PERS laws
* Local or special laws
* Subjects the Constitution bars the Legislature from enacting
* Measures that "deprive" a human being (as defined in statute) of the right to life
* **Ballot access rules:**
* Signatures equal to **10% of active registered voters** collected over 12 months
* **33-1/3% cap** from any single congressional district
* SOS decides sufficiency, with **MS Supreme Court original/exclusive jurisdiction** for challenges
* **Fiscal guardrails:** Sponsors must identify revenue sources; if substantial cost/expenditure, must provide a funding mechanism; cannot redirect funds from one agency to another; cannot require deficit spending.
* **Voting thresholds:**
* Generally: majority approval **and** at least **40% of total votes cast** in that election
* If "substantial cost" initiative: majority approval **and** at least **60% of total votes cast**
* **Legislative involvement option:** Legislature may adopt or amend; if amended, voters see both versions.
* **Governor:** Initiatives are **not subject to gubernatorial veto** and do not require signature.
* **Two-year lock:** No substantive legislative amendment/repeal for **2 years** , unless extenuating circumstances and **3/5 vote** of each chamber.

### Liberty analysis
**Pros (liberty-aligned)**
* **Checks the political class:** Creates a direct mechanism for citizens to override entrenched interests and legislative inaction, consistent with a decentralizing, anti-cartel view of government power.
* **Built-in fiscal restraint features:** Requiring funding identification, restricting deficit spending, and higher thresholds for costly measures reduces the risk of pure "ballot-box budgeting."
* **Statutory-only initiative:** Keeping constitutional amendments off-limits prevents frequent, shifting constitutional policy via campaigns.

**Cons (liberty risks)**
* **Majoritarian risk:** Initiatives can still be used to expand government, regulate, or tax through emotional campaigns and low-information elections.
* **Process restrictions:** The in-state residency requirement for petition circulators and the cap by congressional district can be viewed as participation constraints (even if justified as anti-fraud measures).
* **Two-year lock-in:** Can entrench bad policy temporarily if a poorly drafted initiative passes.

### Recommendation

# Bessent pushes for Powell investigation by Senate Finance Committee
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Senate Republicans[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4fb3c2cc-da52-486d-b036-000bc2086a39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[in a closed-door meeting Wednesday](https://substack.com/redirect/4fb3c2cc-da52-486d-b036-000bc2086a39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to shift the Justice Department's criminal probe of Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over renovation cost overruns **[to a Senate Banking Committee congressional investigation instead.](https://substack.com/redirect/ebca6b55-cb78-4a6a-b747-254305c69cf9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** The proposal aims to satisfy demands for scrutiny while avoiding executive-branch escalation and potentially unblocking stalled Fed nominations.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ebca6b55-cb78-4a6a-b747-254305c69cf9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Congressional Off-Ramp Offered:** Bessent framed the Senate Banking Committee probe as legislative oversight rather than criminal action to reduce distractions and institutional tensions.
* **Tillis Blockade Targeted:** The idea serves as a potential compromise to persuade Sen. Thom Tillis to lift his hold on Federal Reserve nominees tied to resolving the DOJ investigation.
* **Trump 's Scrutiny Demand Met:** Sources note the president seeks an investigation into Powell, with the Banking Committee route seen as satisfying that without DOJ involvement.
* **Powell Testimony Focus:** The underlying issue stems from Powell's 2025 congressional testimony on Federal Reserve headquarters renovation overruns, already under internal inspector general review.

# Trump eyes metals tariff rollback amid House revolt
President Trump is **[planning to scale back steep tariffs on steel and aluminum](https://substack.com/redirect/9ba2c5f2-0e43-4223-8e5a-775bed80f808?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** imports to ease consumer costs and affordability pressures ahead of November midterms, even as the House delivered a rare rebuke by voting to terminate his emergency tariffs on Canada--with six Republicans joining Democrats.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9ba2c5f2-0e43-4223-8e5a-775bed80f808?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Bipartisan House rebukes:** Six Republicans crossed party lines to pass Joint Resolution 72, terminating Trump's national emergency tariffs on Canada despite Speaker Johnson's efforts to block the vote.
**Threats target Canada:** Trump threatened 50% tariffs on Canadian aircraft and 100% retaliatory duties over Canada's China trade deal, impacting companies like Bombardier.
**Exemptions expand deals:** Administration exempted Big Tech firms from chip tariffs, finalized tariff cuts with Taiwan, advanced $550B US-Japan projects, and cut duties on Bangladesh apparel.
**Markets react sharply:** Aluminum prices fell over 2%, Bombardier shares dropped 4.75%, and broader concerns hit autos, luxury goods, and imports, with container volumes down 6.8% in January.

# Venezuela oil billions now flow directly to the US Treasury
U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright announced Thursday that Venezuelan oil sales under Trump administration control have surpassed $1 billion, with[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4fb4c285-872e-41ad-b5ad-52c5a0a82e2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[funds now flowing directly to a U.S. Treasury](https://substack.com/redirect/4fb4c285-872e-41ad-b5ad-52c5a0a82e2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** account instead of a temporary Qatar holding to shield against creditor claims. The shift follows Maduro's capture last month and aims to rebuild the nation's battered energy sector.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4fb4c285-872e-41ad-b5ad-52c5a0a82e2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Revenue Surge Accelerates** : Oil sales controlled by the U.S. have exceeded $1 billion since January, with short-term deals set to deliver another $5 billion in coming months to U.S. refineries and Europe.
* **Qatar Account Scrapped** : Initial $500 million was parked in a U.S.-controlled Qatar account to avoid freezes from Venezuela's massive debt claims, but all future proceeds now go straight to U.S. Treasury.
* **Creditor Risks Loom Large** : Venezuela faces tens of billions in claims from defaults and nationalized assets like those of Exxon Mobil and ConocoPhillips, prompting the temporary offshore workaround.
* **Political Scrutiny Mounts** : Democrats including Schumer and Schiff introduced legislation for an independent audit of the Qatar arrangement amid questions over transparency and government recognition.

Dubai's DP World **[abruptly replaced longtime CEO and chairman](https://substack.com/redirect/5f875a68-5b2d-4b7b-a943-31043ebfd7b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem on Friday after U.S. Department of Justice files revealed his years long friendship with Jeffrey Epstein, including post-conviction contacts and lewd exchanges, prompting major investors to pause new deals with the global logistics powerhouse.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5f875a68-5b2d-4b7b-a943-31043ebfd7b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **Leadership shakeup details:** Yuvraj Narayan, former deputy CEO and CFO since 2005, steps in as Group CEO, while Essa Kazim, ex-Governor of Dubai International Financial Centre, becomes board chairman to drive sustainable growth strategy.
* **Epstein connection revelations:** DOJ documents describe Sulayem as Epstein's "close personal friend" and "trusted" ally, with ongoing exchanges involving business advice, investments, and explicit references to sexual encounters and services.
* **Investor backlash impact:** Canada's La Caisse pension fund, with over $5 billion invested, halted further capital deployment, while British International Investment paused new projects in African ports until DP World addresses the situation.
* **No wrongdoing alleged:** Authorities stress that Epstein file mentions do not prove criminal involvement or participation in blackmail schemes, though Sulayem's ties continued after Epstein's 2008 conviction for soliciting a minor.

# Tax refunds surge 22% higher this season
Average federal **[tax refunds are running 22% higher this early 2026 filing season,](https://substack.com/redirect/a655ceb0-640f-4dae-9807-22b66e8dbb93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Friday, thanks to new tax breaks from President Trump's 2025 legislation that weren't reflected in paycheck withholdings, boosting many Americans' returns amid midterm election buzz.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a655ceb0-640f-4dae-9807-22b66e8dbb93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Refund boost drivers:** New 2025 tax cuts from the "One Big Beautiful Bill" lead to larger refunds since IRS withholding tables stayed unchanged.
* **Historical comparison:** Last year's average refund was around $3,052 through mid-October; experts predict 15-20% overall increases for 2026.
* **Early data caution:** Analysts warn initial figures can mislead as refunds often peak in mid-February due to credits like child and earned income tax credits.
* **Taxpayer variation:** Refund sizes differ widely based on eligibility for breaks, with some seeing hundreds more and others potentially thousands depending on family or income factors.

| | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...

clean_body: | | | | | Peter, | | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud. He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus. He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness. And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible. I saw it up close -- Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything. He started observing the Sabbath. Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance. But as an act of obedience. As a way of saying, " God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped. He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield. No email. No media. No work. He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children. It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much. But over time, it changed him. And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned... This was Charlie's final message. His final act of trust. A book not about politics... but about peace. It 's called: Stop, in the Name of God. Peter, like I mentioned, this isn't a political book. It's not a culture war manifesto. It's a call to stop. To rest. To breathe. To return to God. Because Charlie believed America hadn 't just forgotten truth... It had forgotten trust. Trust that the world keeps spinning when you step away. Trust that God is in control. Trust that rest is not weakness -- it's worship. In Stop, in the Name of God, you'll discover: 🔥 How Charlie reclaimed the Sabbath in a world built on burnout 🔥 What sacred rest gave back to him -- as a father, husband, and believer 🔥 Why he believed this message could spark revival in a restless generation Charlie wrote this book because he knew what it meant to nearly lose his peace -- and what it felt like to find it again. That's the heartbeat of his final message. Charlie Kirk didn't waste his time on earth. He left behind a family. He left behind a movement. And he left behind this truth... For anyone ready to step off the treadmill... and walk back toward what's eternal. Peter, thank you -- in advance -- for helping reach the next generation with truth, faith, and moral courage. These are the very things Charlie gave his life for. May the message he left behind lead you -- just as it led him -- to a deeper trust in God... A stronger love for your family... And a renewed peace in your own soul. name: Adam Schiff
subject: Trump crossed a dangerous line
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY SCHIFF FOR SENATE
body:

# [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=9533%2E5257348%2EsnJ-E7)
** Derek, I want to talk to you about something deeply disturbing, even amidst all of the other horrors of this administration. Donald Trump posted a video so racist that even Republicans publicly condemned it, and he ultimately took it down. The video depicted President and First Lady Obama as apes. _I’m not going to share the screenshot of the Obamas, but it’s vile, and you may have seen it already. We cannot become numb to this.__**We just can’t.**_ Yes, this is Trump’s usual AI-generated garbage: racist, insulting, juvenile, and designed to inflame. But this one crossed an especially dangerous line. It wasn’t just a dog whistle. It was open, dehumanizing racism, posted by the sitting president of the United States. I’m in the video too, portrayed as a giraffe alongside J.B Pritzker: [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=.zL8wZO&refcode=&t=4&akid=9533%2E5257348%2EsnJ-E7) Normally, I brush off this kind of nonsense. Trump’s insults are ridiculous, and he thrives on attention. But the racism in this video directed at the Obamas is too extreme, too explicit, and too dangerous to ignore. This is who he is. And this is how authoritarian movements operate: distract, degrade, dehumanize – especially when things are going badly. Because here’s the reality Trump wants to distract us from: His economy is failing as Americans struggle to find a good paying job. Prices are going up. There is blood on the streets, the result of his murderous immigration policies. People are fed up. And his political support is falling fast. So he reaches for the oldest, ugliest weapon in the playbook — blatant racism — hoping it will divide us, exhaust us, or scare us into silence. **It can’t. It won’t. And we can’t let it.** We can stop him. We can reject this bigotry and deal his failed agenda a decisive blow by flipping the House and the Senate in November. Accountability is coming, but only if we do the work to make it happen. [_**If you’re with me, please chip in today. With power changing hands after the midterms, we will have oversight, and with oversight comes consequences.**_](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/5660?t=5&akid=9533%2E5257348%2EsnJ-E7) ** | [ DONATE ](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/5660?t=6&akid=9533%2E5257348%2EsnJ-E7)
---
**
Trump continues to tell us exactly who he is. It’s long past time for Republicans to believe him.
Thank you for staying engaged, paying attention, and refusing to look away.
Adam

| | **Last week, I introduced the Mammography Access for Veterans Act.** This bipartisan legislation would expand veterans' access to lifesaving breast cancer screenings through the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). Women are the fastest-growing group in the veteran population. As the number of women veterans rapidly increases, VA must continue to modernize its women's health care services. **This bill is one step toward ensuring women veterans around the country have access to lifesaving, preventative screenings for breast cancer.** During my time in Congress, I have hosted more than 70 forums to hear directly from Northwest Washington state veterans about their needs, including five roundtables in September 2025. Following those conversations in September, I published 'Listening to Veterans in Northwest Washington,' a report capturing local veterans' most pressing challenges and outlining policy recommendations for Congress and VA to address these concerns. I submitted this report to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (HVAC) to ensure Northwest Washington veterans' voices impact the policy-making process. **Northwest Washington is home to nearly 57,000 veterans, including many veterans who served in Iraq and Afghanistan.** I am committed to ensuring that the women and men who have served our country in uniform get the resources and services they need – whether it be healthcare, housing, or career training. **I will always work for the veterans of Northwest Washington. Peter,

Some days, it feels like everything in our politics is loud, chaotic, and
designed to wear you down.

Corporate PACs flex their checkbooks. Billionaires try to buy outcomes.
And the people actually fighting for the right things are expected to
just... keep up somehow.

I won’t pretend that it doesn’t get frustrating. It does.

But here’s what I’ve learned from every movement that’s ever achieved
something real: Lasting change doesn’t come from a single moment. It comes
from people who show up consistently and refuse to give up, even when it
seems like the odds are stacked against them.

One way to create that consistency is through our recurring donor program.
Over 2,300 people have stepped up to contribute to this campaign each
month, and being able to count on this support is huge.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/543?c0=em-ms-aes-20260213-1-ak.MSzr-g&amount=10&refcode=em20260213-1695&t=1004&akid=1701%2E251025%2EnYaYjm ]Today, I’m hoping you’ll join them and become a recurring donor to fuel
our campaign each month.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/543?c0=em-ms-aes-20260213-1-ak.MSzr-g&amount=10&refcode=em20260213-1695&t=1023&akid=1701%2E251025%2EnYaYjm ]Donate monthly ››

Any bit of stability goes a long way in a race as competitive as ours —
especially right now. Here are a few reasons why:

* Our primary is just six months away, and the decisions we make now
shape whether we’re ready for the final stretch.
* Monthly support lets us plan instead of scrambling. It means hiring
organizers earlier, locking in events, and building real momentum
without a lack of resources holding us back.
* It keeps us accountable to people, not corporate PACs or AIPAC. We
don’t take their money. I’m the only candidate in this race who never
has, and never will. That means this campaign only works if it’s
powered by folks who believe in it enough to stick around.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/543?c0=em-ms-aes-20260213-1-ak.MSzr-g&amount=10&refcode=em20260213-1695&t=1024&akid=1701%2E251025%2EnYaYjm ]If you’re able, please start a recurring contribution of any amount
today and help us build an unstoppable movement.

Thanks for standing with me in this fight. It means more than you know.

In solidarity,

Abdul

P.S. I know a monthly commitment isn’t possible for everyone. If that’s
the case for you right now, [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/979?amount=10&refcode=em20260213-1695&t=1025&akid=1701%2E251025%2EnYaYjm ]a one-time gift still helps us keep moving
forward — and I’m so grateful for it.

name: Gov. Andy Beshear
subject: I can't and won't stay silent about what ICE is doing.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by In This Together PAC
body:
[PETITION]
Peter,

_**What we're seeing right now from the Department of Homeland Security and ICE should concern every American who believes in the rule of law.**_

Across the country, ICE agents are operating without basic safeguards that are supposed to protect both the public and law enforcement officers themselves.

They are operating with no legal warrants, no accountability, and harmful tactics that create fear in our communities at the cost of American lives.

As a former state attorney general, I can't look at this and stay quiet. Law enforcement has immense power — and with that power comes responsibility. Officers must be trained, supervised, and held accountable to clear legal standards. That's not optional, **it's the foundation of public trust.**

But right now, that foundation is cracking. **The way ICE agents have behaved in Minneapolis and elsewhere doesn’t meet the standards for how any law enforcement agency should conduct itself.** The result? There is now a body count of American citizens because of ICE’s actions in Minnesota.

**That's why I'm calling for immediate action, Peter.**

Every ICE agent in every city across the U.S. needs to be withdrawn, so agents can be re-trained and directed to act within the law, follow proper procedures, and prioritize safety and de-escalation. And we need real accountability at the top — that means leadership that makes it clear that no one is above the law, including people working for the federal government.

Welcome to Michaela For Tennessee
Don't recognize this sender? [Unsubscribe with one click](https://substack..4P6ztYdhiA3IdgvKvjr5oYK81I-wUtfsWT2o3sEY9aU?)
Michaela for Tennessee recently imported your email address from another platform to Substack. You'll now receive their posts via email or the [Substack app](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4f77445b-378e-46c4-ba85-d3546e8ecddc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). To set up your profile and discover more on Substack, [click here](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/9fcdc51c-fb53-4281-b3a7-95a0439afb72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
I was working in Congress when Donald Trump was elected. We had all hoped beyond hope that he wouldn't win, or if he did win, that Democrats would at least have control of the House of Representatives to hold him in check.
We all know those hopes didn't come to pass.
After the election, we had two-and-a-half months to prepare. We knew their plans ([Project 2025](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e57794b7-78dd-42f9-8fc4-10b4bf2bac7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), despite Trump's best efforts to disavow his connection as the unpopularity of what they proposed became evident). We even knew that they would try to overwhelm all of us by "flooding the zone", which they have flaunted as their strategy for years.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a7540de7-b489-48c4-a4cd-4523c9d3dc7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But when inauguration day came, I felt like I was paddling a life boat when what we needed were combat ships. (The potential for maritime metaphors is rich. Sometimes I feel like the "wait out the Trump Presidency" strategy employed by some of our leaders is like building an arc and closing the door while the flood waters rise around the rest of us).
And y'all, their flood the zone strategy has never stopped. Do you feel absolutely overwhelmed? Unable to focus on one bad thing? Often hopeless? They're just going to keep opening the dam and letting the floodwaters rush in, without a moments' respite.
This week, amidst a to-do list that never stops growing, I thought of the following, pressing topics I wanted to break down for you all. In no particular order: [the SAVE Act.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d4c31e5a-a7cb-4ae7-a948-76d0f6689e56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The depravity and corruption revealed in the[ latest Epstein Files release](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0443f024-2086-4ecb-8d99-1af9956e9b5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [Bondi's disastrous hearing](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/3661c199-cfcd-49a8-8db8-7bcfd93071d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Revoking the [endangerment finding](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1df12152-2464-4ec0-b655-13dacba8b9d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [Democrats' DHS demands](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/654fc5c6-e766-4727-9a60-f30af4ac3d5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
They want us scattered, unfocused, and isolated. They would love it if we were all just clinging to debris, unable to see through the fog.
**While they try to distract us, terrorize us, and divide us, we have to organize. We have 262 days until midterms, when we have the chance to take back the House, hold wrongdoers accountable, and start building a government that actually serves us.**
**What does it look like to build a ship instead of clinging to driftwood?**
Right now, my campaign has [365 volunteers](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/2f4b3c13-d126-47a9-bd8a-05b6b3ef2158?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). We've started [weekly phone banking](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/24ae179a-7b80-49b8-bd61-5b9396f2f24f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). We start canvassing (knocking on doors) next month. We need 1.1 million voter touches in the next 9 months if we're going to flip this thing.
But we're not just focused on my race: we're planning to run a coordinated campaign and increase participation at every level of the ballot.
A coordinated campaign is exactly what it sounds like. We're are going to coordinate, share resources, and build together with candidates up and down the ballot, not work by ourselves in isolation towards the same goal.
Here's one scenario: an 8% increase in Democratic turnout in August (which is my primary election, currently uncontested, but the general election for our county races) doesn't just help my race. It flips Knox County Commission and School Board seats. It makes the mayor's race competitive. It wins critical Blount County Commission seats. It helps us gain ground in Loudon, Campbell, Grainger, Claiborne, Union, Jefferson. An 8% increase in Democratic voter turnout is completely achievable - and so is much, much more.
**They want to overwhelm us so we can 't do anything to stop them. **
**But we 're not going to be distracted. My team and I are focused on building campaign infrastructure that outlasts this election cycle and creates generations of organizers who know how to win in red territory.**
To run a field program capable of flipping an entire congressional district--and delivering down-ballot wins even if we fall short at the top--we need to raise $250,000. That's not our full budget. That's _just_ field: the doorknocking, phonebanking, relational organizing, voter registration, early vote mobilization, and election day operations that turn people into supporters and supporters into voters.
Even if you're skeptical that TN-02 can flip in 2026 (though I promise you, _**it can**_), your investment still delivers wins. Knox County can go blue. Our school board could flip. Local red districts can become purple. And in 2028 (and 2030, and beyond) we'll have an army of trained organizers and proven infrastructure ready to scale and outlast any flood waters they unleash.
**We have 262 days until midterms. 174 days until the August elections.**
**[Will you invest in building the ship we need](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4953e239-ce5f-41a6-b408-b42a3243f1d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)?**
One more note - many of our counties are still recruiting candidates to run for office! Feb. 19th is the deadline to get on local and municipal ballots. If you're on the fence, I encourage you to give voters an option and not let the GOP run uncontested. Make them spend money, time, and resources. Feel free to reply to this email if you're curious or have questions.
Let's keep building,
Michaela

name: Lindsey Graham
subject: High stakes
body:
The Left is flooding this race with cash. |
---
Fellow American,

I'm not going to waste your time.

We are falling behind - right now.

My liberal opponent outraised us last quarter, and the consequences are serious. This isn't about headlines or bragging rights. _It's about what happens next if we don't act immediately._

Non-stop attack ads all over South Carolina attacking me and President Trump.
Money from California, New York, and DC trying to distort my conservative record.
Hollywood elites buying this race.
**If we let that stand, we risk losing ground we cannot afford to lose.**

The Left is desperate to take me out because they know I'll stand my ground. They know I won't cave. And they know I will always stand with President Trump.

Liam Conejo Ramos – the 5-year-old boy detained by ICE – is out of detention and back home. Thankfully.
I’m deeply relieved and grateful to everyone who spoke up, showed up, and refused to let his detention go unnoticed.
But the only reason he was there in the first place was because of a paperwork problem.
Meanwhile, billionaires and giant corporations use the fine print to break the law, trample our rights, and gain power every single day . That contrast tells you everything you need to know about our country’s two-tiered system of justice, one that’s ruthless toward the vulnerable and endlessly forgiving to the powerful.
It’s why I’m running for attorney general.
We can’t look the other way when ICE agents or corporations violate our laws. Systems built on fear, detention, and family separation cannot be fixed at the margins. ICE must be abolished . [https://secure.ngpvan.com/xKCuI2hxU0akC8u5HegFxQ2]
Liam is free today because people refused to accept injustice as inevitable. That’s what gives me hope. But for every Liam who makes it home, there are so many others still trapped in detention, waiting for someone to fight for them.

And thank you for being part of this fight.

clean_body: [] Liam Conejo Ramos – the 5-year-old boy detained by ICE – is out of detention and back home. Thankfully. I’m deeply relieved and grateful to everyone who spoke up, showed up, and refused to let his detention go unnoticed. But the only reason he was there in the first place was because of a paperwork problem. Meanwhile, billionaires and giant corporations use the fine print to break the law, trample our rights, and gain power every single day . That contrast tells you everything you need to know about our country’s two-tiered system of justice, one that’s ruthless toward the vulnerable and endlessly forgiving to the powerful. It’s why I’m running for attorney general. We can’t look the other way when ICE agents or corporations violate our laws. Systems built on fear, detention, and family separation cannot be fixed at the margins. ICE must be abolished . [] Liam is free today because people refused to accept injustice as inevitable. That’s what gives me hope. But for every Liam who makes it home, there are so many others still trapped in detention, waiting for someone to fight for them. ADD YOUR NAME to our petition demanding accountability when ICE agents violate state law and an end to a system that views cruelty as policy. [] ADD YOUR NAME [] I’m running to build a justice system that actually lives up to its name. Thank you for standing with Liam. Thank you for standing against "paperwork" that strips people of their rights. And thank you for being part of this fight. With gratitude, David Seligman [] As Executive Director of the nonprofit legal organization Towards Justice, David has taken on corporate giants like Amazon, Uber, and the biggest corporate landlords in the country—helping recover more than $70 million stolen from working people by powerful interests. Now he’s running for attorney general to defend our freedoms, challenge concentrated power, and build a future where working people can thrive. He’s already doing the work. Once again, Trump’s Department of Education is trying to withhold billions of dollars in federal funding from California schools in its latest attempt to impose its hateful, extreme, anti-trans agenda.
So once again, I took him to court. And just last night — within 24 hours of filing the lawsuit — I secured a temporary order blocking this unlawful funding cut.
This lawless administration is attempting to terminate nearly $5 billion in federal funding on entirely baseless claims.
Using our classrooms, teachers, and students as leverage to intimidate California’s education agencies is wrong, and it’s unlawful. I’m going to keep fighting this in the courts until we win.
If you support this work to hold Trump and his administration accountable, please consider donating any amount to my re-election campaign today so we can keep it going through Trump’s entire second term. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?amount=50]
Trump’s Department of Education is trying to use this education funding to coerce schools into adopting policies that would forcibly out transgender students and violate their privacy.
California is fully compliant with federal privacy laws, and the administration hasn’t identified a single case where a school denied parents access to student records.
But still, they’re trying to twist the law to suit their liking and impose new conditions that Congress never approved — holding billions of dollars in education funding hostage in the process.
Schools should be places of learning and safety, not political battlegrounds. That’s why I took Trump to court. I’m asking for a permanent injunction to stop this power grab for good before it causes real harm.
When Trump threatens education funding, he’s threatening kids, teachers, and families — and he’s doing it to advance a discriminatory political agenda.
I won’t stand by while the federal government bullies California schools, undermines student privacy, or puts LGBTQ+ kids at risk.
But taking on this administration requires resources, focus, and the ability to fight back fast. I’m running for re-election so I can keep standing up for California — and I need your help to do it.
Help us keep fighting these critical battles by chipping in today. Your support directly powers my work to hold Trump accountable and stop him from breaking the law at the expense of California’s students. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?amount=50]

clean_body: [] Once again, Trump’s Department of Education is trying to withhold billions of dollars in federal funding from California schools in its latest attempt to impose its hateful, extreme, anti-trans agenda. So once again, I took him to court. And just last night — within 24 hours of filing the lawsuit — I secured a temporary order blocking this unlawful funding cut. This lawless administration is attempting to terminate nearly $5 billion in federal funding on entirely baseless claims. Using our classrooms, teachers, and students as leverage to intimidate California’s education agencies is wrong, and it’s unlawful. I’m going to keep fighting this in the courts until we win. If you support this work to hold Trump and his administration accountable, please consider donating any amount to my re-election campaign today so we can keep it going through Trump’s entire second term. [] Trump’s Department of Education is trying to use this education funding to coerce schools into adopting policies that would forcibly out transgender students and violate their privacy. California is fully compliant with federal privacy laws, and the administration hasn’t identified a single case where a school denied parents access to student records. But still, they’re trying to twist the law to suit their liking and impose new conditions that Congress never approved — holding billions of dollars in education funding hostage in the process. Schools should be places of learning and safety, not political battlegrounds. That’s why I took Trump to court. I’m asking for a permanent injunction to stop this power grab for good before it causes real harm. When Trump threatens education funding, he’s threatening kids, teachers, and families — and he’s doing it to advance a discriminatory political agenda. I won’t stand by while the federal government bullies California schools, undermines student privacy, or puts LGBTQ+ kids at risk. But taking on this administration requires resources, focus, and the ability to fight back fast. I’m running for re-election so I can keep standing up for California — and I need your help to do it. Help us keep fighting these critical battles by chipping in today. Your support directly powers my work to hold Trump accountable and stop him from breaking the law at the expense of California’s students. body:
They’re coming for your wallet — again

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | |
While I’m in Washington, DC fighting to lower costs for families, Democrats in Olympia are doing the exact opposite.
Last year, far-left legislators in Olympia passed the largest tax increase in Washington state history — nearly $10 billion in new taxes and fees that hit working families right where it hurts:
* Gas tax increase — 6 cents per gallon, with automatic increases still to come
* Property taxes — a 55% expansion in local school levy authority, paving the way for higher property taxes
* Business tax increases — punishing the job creators who employ our neighbors
* Hunting and fishing licenses — up 38%
* Discover Pass — up 50%

And they’re not done.
This session, Democrats went even further — introducing **Senate Bill 6346 on February 4** , which would impose a **9.9% income tax on higher earners** , blowing a hole through Washington’s long-standing ban on income taxes. Once the door is open, working families are next.
This is exactly why we need strong conservative voices in Congress.
The federal government is putting in place guardrails to keep state governments like the one in Olympia from veering completely to the far-left socialist agenda that we’re seeing in New York City and San Francisco.
We’re fighting hard to ensure voter integrity, prevent waste and fraud, and stop policies that distort higher education and enable homelessness.

body:
Trump Excludes Polis From White House Governors Meeting
| | | | [](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/scs6231c813)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s4oc88070eb)**
| | Hi friends,
It’s tonight. In just a few hours, **[Republican candidates](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s7h086c2bc8) will step onto the stage in Durango** — and the questions driving this forum came from you.
TABOR. Illegal immigration. Election safeguards. Parental rights. The limits of state power.
This isn’t a campaign stop. **It’s a live forum shaped by voters across Colorado.**
**We’ll be livestreaming the entire event on the RMV YouTube** channel and amplifying it across our social platforms.
If you can’t be in the room, you can still be in the conversation.
👉**Watch live[here](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/sane21cbf77)**
Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏛️ **Under the Golden Dome...** Lawmakers are [testing TABOR’s limits again](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s7jfae3e1bc) with Senate Bill 42, which critics say would reclassify revenue to avoid voter-approved caps and retain more excess funds instead of issuing refunds—reviving concerns about bypassing taxpayer consent. Meanwhile, a bipartisan [resolution to boost road funding](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s1l82aa83a5) cleared committee as lawmakers acknowledged deteriorating infrastructure and frustration that past transportation promises haven’t delivered. At the same time, an emotional debate is unfolding [over sentencing for child traffickers](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s3h4f87a631), as legislators weigh proposals to raise mandatory minimum penalties and limit probation for buyers, with survivors arguing current law allows offenders to “walk free” while victims carry lifelong scars.
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Colorado confirmed it [shares certain Medicaid data](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s6if390511e) with the federal government, complicating immigration and privacy debates. Denver advanced a proposal to ban ICE agents and other officers [from wearing masks](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s6v3a0eb416) during operations, sparking competing concerns over safety and transparency. President Trump announced [Gov. Jared Polis wasn't invited](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s4i93fd189e) to an upcoming White House governors’ meeting, heightening political tensions. Federal prosecutors also filed charges in two cases alleging more than [$4 million in fraudulent Medicaid](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/sdqf5e0dfca) ride billing, raising oversight questions. And at Colorado Mesa University, TPUSA student moderators [pressed gubernatorial hopefuls](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/sasaa83f8ed) on TABOR, energy reliability, and rural control as the 2026 race heats up.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** A heated House Judiciary hearing put the [Biden-era DOJ under scrutiny](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/sem77d2b315) as Rep. Brandon Gill (R-TX) delivered rapid-fire questioning on the Mar-a-Lago raid, surveillance of Republicans, investigations into parents and pro-life Catholics, and the DOJ’s January 6 actions.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** One piece argues Colorado Republicans can learn from Super Bowl discipline—[winning requires fundamentals](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s3ib1051389), not hype. Another questions the [long-term costs](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s1g0d244d86) of wolf reintroduction, pointing to livestock losses and a growing urban-rural divide over conservation policy.
This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, February 13, 2026.
– Team RMV

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Trump Excludes Polis From White House Governors Meeting](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s2j6cf4955e)** [KDVR](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/sdi5031ef4d)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s5kafeda711)
****President Donald Trump posted on Wednesday that two Democratic governors will not be invited to a bipartisan meeting and dinner next week. Gov. Jared Polis is one of them.
“The invitations were sent to ALL Governors, other than two, who I feel are not worthy of being there,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, referring to Polis and Governor Wes Moore of Maryland.
Trump said Polis was not invited to the governors’ meeting since former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters is serving her prison sentence. The post comes after Trump has repeatedly called for the release of former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters, who was convicted for her role in a 2021 election security breach.
On Wednesday, a spokesperson with Polis’ office provided a statement, which did not specifically address whether the governor had received an invitation.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s7nb41ab3bf)**
|
---
**[$4 million-plus in alleged Medicaid ride billing draws federal fraud charges in Colorado](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s3o5c5ed4b7)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s7p59e123c9)
* **$4M+ in alleged Medicaid ride fraud charged** – Federal prosecutors filed fraud and money laundering charges in two separate cases involving non-emergency medical transportation billing in Mesa and Douglas counties, alleging over $4 million in improper claims. Authorities say the reimbursement-based system was manipulated through inflated mileage, duplicate billing, and rides that allegedly never occurred.
* ******Mesa County indictment details family-linked billing** – One defendant is accused of billing roughly $1 million in Medicaid transportation claims, including hundreds of thousands of dollars tied to rides for family members that allegedly did not match actual medical appointments.
* ******Douglas County case alleges $3.3M scheme** – A second indictment claims more than $3 million in fraudulent billing tied to a single beneficiary and other questionable claims, with prosecutors alleging funds were used for personal purchases rather than patient transport.

**[CMU student leaders press governor hopefuls on taxes, energy and rural control](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s1n4afebef4)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s0kb0ba42e9)
* _****_**Students Press Governor Hopefuls on Taxes and Rural Control** – At a Colorado Mesa University forum, GOP gubernatorial candidates were challenged by student leaders on TABOR, budget deficits, and whether Colorado has a revenue or spending problem, with several arguing the state faces overspending, hidden transfers, and “shell game” budgeting rather than a revenue shortage.__

* _****_**Energy Reliability and PUC Authority in Focus** – Candidates sharply criticized current energy policies, with calls to overhaul Public Utilities Commission leadership, restore dispatchable power sources, and prioritize grid reliability over climate mandates they say are weakening Colorado’s electric stability.__

* _****_**Rural Water Rights and Local Control Defended** – On land and water policy, hopefuls emphasized protecting private property rights, prioritizing agricultural water use, and pushing back against state mandates they argue are eroding rural autonomy and shifting costs onto local communities.__

**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[Buyers walk free, survivors carry the scars: Colorado debates sentencing for child traffickers](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s3ic48f8375)** **BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | FEBRUARY 13** Colorado lawmakers confronted a question this week that has lingered for years under the gold dome: how far should the state go in punishing those who buy and traffic children? Two bills offered two different answers. [Senate Bill 26-015](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s6s12822e38) cleared Senate Judiciary on a 6–1 vote and was referred, as amended, to Appropriations. Senator Nick Hinrichsen cast the lone “no.” [HB26-1082](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s4r508b887a) went the other direction. Representative Scott Bottoms’ bill would have required life without parole in certain cases involving trafficked minors. It stalled in the House Judiciary Committee.
**[What SuperBowl LX Can Teach Us About Colorado Politics](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/sch55dc91eb)** **BY RUSS MINARY | COMMENTARY | FEBRUARY 12** _Last Sunday, millions of Americans watched one of the most lackluster competitions between two NFL teams in a long while. The stats indicate that the Seattle Seahawks outplayed the New England Patriots, consistently from start to finish. The score speaks clearlly: Seattle won and New England lost. I think SuperBowl LX was chock full of lessons that apply to Colorado politics._
**[When grievance overrides justice: The risk of declaring nothing illegal](https://link.email.joinrmv.-DKQ/s3ta15dd0b0)** **BY MICHAEL HANCOCK | COMMENTARY | FEBRUARY 11** _“There is no such thing as illegal on stolen land.” It is a clever slogan—short, moral, and absolute. And like most slogans that aspire to absoluteness, it collapses the moment it is treated as an argument rather than a chant. The claim rests on a simple premise: because land was once taken unjustly, no law exercised upon it today can be legitimate. The conclusion sounds radical, even righteous. In reality, it is neither._

Brandon Gill (R-TX) delivered rapid-fire questioning on the Mar-a-Lago raid, surveillance of Republicans, investigations into parents and pro-life Catholics, and the DOJ’s January 6 actions. 🗣️ Commentary Spotlight... One piece argues Colorado Republicans can learn from Super Bowl discipline—, not hype. Another questions the of wolf reintroduction, pointing to livestock losses and a growing urban-rural divide over conservation policy. This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, February 13, 2026. – Team RMV | TODAY'S TOP STORIES **President Donald Trump posted on Wednesday that two Democratic governors will not be invited to a bipartisan meeting and dinner next week. Gov. Jared Polis is one of them. “The invitations were sent to ALL Governors, other than two, who I feel are not worthy of being there,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, referring to Polis and Governor Wes Moore of Maryland. Trump said Polis was not invited to the governors’ meeting since former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters is serving her prison sentence. The post comes after Trump has repeatedly called for the release of former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters, who was convicted for her role in a 2021 election security breach. On Wednesday, a spokesperson with Polis’ office provided a statement, which did not specifically address whether the governor had received an invitation. | BY SHAINA COLE, $4M+ in alleged Medicaid ride fraud charged – Federal prosecutors filed fraud and money laundering charges in two separate cases involving non-emergency medical transportation billing in Mesa and Douglas counties, alleging over $4 million in improper claims. Authorities say the reimbursement-based system was manipulated through inflated mileage, duplicate billing, and rides that allegedly never occurred. **Mesa County indictment details family-linked billing – One defendant is accused of billing roughly $1 million in Medicaid transportation claims, including hundreds of thousands of dollars tied to rides for family members that allegedly did not match actual medical appointments. **Douglas County case alleges $3.3M scheme – A second indictment claims more than $3 million in fraudulent billing tied to a single beneficiary and other questionable claims, with prosecutors alleging funds were used for personal purchases rather than patient transport. | The Rocky Mountain Voice is a 501(c)(3) that exists to promote informed civic engagement and the principles of self-governance through enterprise reporting on public policy, politics, government, and culture throughout the state of Colorado. The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support! | BY JEN SCHUMANN, Students Press Governor Hopefuls on Taxes and Rural Control – At a Colorado Mesa University forum, GOP gubernatorial candidates were challenged by student leaders on TABOR, budget deficits, and whether Colorado has a revenue or spending problem, with several arguing the state faces overspending, hidden transfers, and “shell game” budgeting rather than a revenue shortage. **Energy Reliability and PUC Authority in Focus – Candidates sharply criticized current energy policies, with calls to overhaul Public Utilities Commission leadership, restore dispatchable power sources, and prioritize grid reliability over climate mandates they say are weakening Colorado’s electric stability. **Rural Water Rights and Local Control Defended – On land and water policy, hopefuls emphasized protecting private property rights, prioritizing agricultural water use, and pushing back against state mandates they argue are eroding rural autonomy and shifting costs onto local communities. | ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | FEBRUARY 13 Colorado lawmakers confronted a question this week that has lingered for years under the gold dome: how far should the state go in punishing those who buy and traffic children? Two bills offered two different answers. cleared Senate Judiciary on a 6–1 vote and was referred, as amended, to Appropriations. Senator Nick Hinrichsen cast the lone “no.” went the other direction. Representative Scott Bottoms’ bill would have required life without parole in certain cases involving trafficked minors. It stalled in the House Judiciary Committee. BY RUSS MINARY | COMMENTARY | FEBRUARY 12 Last Sunday, millions of Americans watched one of the most lackluster competitions between two NFL teams in a long while. The stats indicate that the Seattle Seahawks outplayed the New England Patriots, consistently from start to finish. The score speaks clearlly: Seattle won and New England lost. I think SuperBowl LX was chock full of lessons that apply to Colorado politics. BY MICHAEL HANCOCK | COMMENTARY | FEBRUARY 11 “There is no such thing as illegal on stolen land.” It is a clever slogan—short, moral, and absolute. And like most slogans that aspire to absoluteness, it collapses the moment it is treated as an argument rather than a chant. The claim rests on a simple premise: because land was once taken unjustly, no law exercised upon it today can be legitimate. The conclusion sounds radical, even righteous. In reality, it is neither. Peter,
There’s only two weeks left in this year’s short legislative session and there’s a lot on the line. We’re in the Capitol every day working to pass our priorities all the while defending against threats to our environment.
In order to continue making progress and defend against threats to our environment, we need you , Peter.
We have a chance this session to make important progress by passing 1.25% for Wildlife and securing critical wildlife and habitat funding, passing a monumental bill to make polluters pay for the damage they’ve done to our environment, and passing a strong budget to fund new progress and existing programs.
To defend what we’ve achieved and to keep pushing forward, we need more resources [https://secure.ngpvan.com/i_-oa1WQ0keSurrrDjgtSg2] . More capacity. More support behind this work at a moment when it matters most.
Give now [https://secure.everyaction.com/YnnBhNxoe0-gdDf_E1iL8Q2?am=20&contactdata=XK32quFqpwA96miswKpuqWr+kDbUSfd+7JrvEe4c1ptjd7BLnsci+9TOCeJtEIU4Ao6w9P52/FgHmhS2/6H7AmaxagAykiMGBVrXaEvfpqY4N48uwE1k6oaguCgVTs/n]
Unfortunately, we’re also being forced to spend too much time - especially in a fast-moving short session - defending against threats to our climate and environment. We’re fighting four Major Threats, including a bill that threatens Oregon’s land use planning system. Future generations of Oregonians are depending on us to protect the way of life that we cherish, our clean water, and our climate, and more.
If you’re able, please make a contribution of $50 today to allow us to recruit 3 new volunteers for an upcoming advocacy day [https://secure.ngpvan.com/i_-oa1WQ0keSurrrDjgtSg2] . Your support helps ensure we can protect progress and continue fighting for a climate-safe, just future.

Thank you for standing with us,

name: Deb Haaland
subject: update on our race in New Mexico
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
This is going to be a tough race.

| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/1102?refcode=jtk263-fr-nd&t=1&akid=7444%2E400544%2EPliHcn)
---
Friend, I had to share this news right away.
**There are now FIVE Republicans running to flip New Mexico.** Several of them are using their own wealth to try to buy this race and bring an extreme agenda into our state.
_One self-funded multimillionaire GOP candidate has even said he’ll put $2 MILLION of his own money into his campaign._
I urgently need your grassroots support to ensure my campaign can compete. _**[So please, will you chip in $5 right now to help me close the gap on my $50,000 goal and win in New Mexico?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5112?refcode=jtk263-fr-nd&amount=5&t=2&akid=7444%2E400544%2EPliHcn)**_
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5112?refcode=jtk263-fr-nd&t=3&akid=7444%2E400544%2EPliHcn)
---
**I’ll be honest: This is going to be a tough race.** It's already clear that the GOP is going to try to buy this race, and unlike my multimillionaire opponent, I can't just write myself a check.
I don’t come from wealth, friend. I have never had the means to self-fund a campaign, unlike my wealthy opponents. I was a single mom living paycheck to paycheck, relying on government programs like SNAP, WIC, and Medicaid to help keep my child fed and healthy.
**So I know what it's like to struggle, and I also know that it takes a village, in both life and in politics. I strongly believe leaders should make people’s lives easier, not harder. We all want good roads, safe communities, strong education, access to parks, and affordable, healthy food to eat.**
That’s exactly why I’m better prepared to lead. I understand affordability because I’ve lived it. I know how critical strong public schools, accessible health care, and safe communities are because my family relied on them. These issues aren’t abstract to me, they’re personal. And beyond my lived experience, I’ve led at the highest levels of government, serving in Congress and as U.S. Secretary of the Interior, where I took on tough fights and delivered real results for communities across the country. I know how to fight for working families — and how to get things done.
Experience matters. Leadership matters. And I’m ready.
That's why I’m running to be the next governor of New Mexico, to build a better future for working families. But I need your help to reach my midnight fundraising goal to make that a reality:
**I'm running a people-powered campaign that relies on grassroots support from folks like you chipping in $5, $10, or whatever you can spare to help me go up against these self-funded multimillionaires.**_**[Please, will you chip in to help me win and keep New Mexico blue?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5112?refcode=jtk263-fr-nd&t=4&akid=7444%2E400544%2EPliHcn)**_
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [Donate $10](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5113?refcode=jtk263-fr-nd&t=5&akid=7444%2E400544%2EPliHcn)

Deb

But fighting back against this kind of retaliation is expensive by design.

| | There's a lot to be outraged about in Washington right now. Trump has slowly eroded our rights, expanded executive power, and spent your taxpayer money on pet projects that benefit his wealthy friends. While outrage is useful as motivation, it alone won't stop Trump's abuse of power. **Accountability does.** Under Donald Trump, we've seen federal agencies weaponized, constitutional rights trampled, and billions of dollars doled out to Trump's priorities with no meaningful oversight. **The question isn't whether this is wrong — it's whether we have leaders who will actually do something about it.** Here's what I've been fighting for in the Senate:
* As Ranking Member of the Senate Budget Committee, I led the fight against the Republican "Big, Ugly Betrayal" budget — a package that funneled nearly **$75 billion in slush funds to ICE and another $70 billion to CBP** with little oversight or accountability.

* I've been a leading voice in demanding **ethics and accountability reforms** after repeated abuses by Trump's cronies. From legislation to end Trump's crypto corruption, to a bill to hold ICE and CBP accountable when they violate our rights, I am fighting to rein Trump in.

* I've been a strong supporter of efforts to **strengthen the War Powers Act** and push back when presidents try to bypass Congress and the Constitution to start wars without authorization.

**These are real fights to put guardrails back on executive power.** And here's the truth: the Republican forces pushing authoritarianism are well-funded, organized, and relentless. Peter, it's George Latimer. During these past few months, I’ve heard the same stories from folks across Westchester and the Bronx: people are working hard to provide for their families, and doing everything right — but costs have skyrocketed and the bills can feel never ending. So I was shocked when I heard Donald Trump’s latest message on affordability: [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125339132/601465013/126481460?amount=10&source=GL_EM_FR_021326_B1_MM01&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQwMzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDE2NTRjZjktMTkwOS1mMTExLTgzMmUtMDAyMjQ4MmE5NzMzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=sKBMZkmJ3tCoq2RD5_JZxeILhWrHDaGju_Vg2B659pI=) In the midst of Trump’s affordability crisis — _caused by his administration's policies_ — he’s speaking out _against_ lowering the cost of housing. Peter, this is a slap in the face to every American struggling to keep the lights on, put food on the table, or pay for their medications. Peter,
I wanted to emphasize just how serious of a moment we are in.
Donald Trump’s federal agents are going door to door in Minnesota looking for folks based on their accent or color of their skin. Kids are afraid to go to school, small businesses are hurting, another life has been lost, and the people responsible have yet to be held accountable. Instead, Donald Trump’s DOJ is investigating me.
Why? Because my focus has always been protecting the people of Minnesota.
They’re trying to scare me and our state — but Minnesota will not be intimidated into silence and neither will I. This legal battle will be expensive, that’s why they’re doing this. They want me to back down and surrender, but I won’t.

body:
I keep hearing the same thing: people are feeling squeezed by rising costs. Peter,

From St. Louis County and St. Louis City to our small towns and rural communities, I'm hearing the same thing from Missourians: **life is getting more expensive, and _families are feeling squeezed_.**

Groceries cost more.

Gas costs more.

Rent and utilities keep going up.

And the job market isn't what it needs to be for folks to keep up.

For too many Missourians, it feels like they're doing everything right — working hard, playing by the rules — and still falling further behind.**That's not right, and it's not what opportunity is supposed to look like,_especially not in the wealthiest nation on earth_. **

Trump and his allies keep protecting special interests, undermining working people, and creating more chaos instead of offering real solutions for ACTUAL people. That kind of "leadership" makes everyday life harder for folks here at home.

**[I am fighting for policies that put money back in people's pockets, invest in good-paying jobs, and make sure no one has to choose between paying the bills and caring for their family. If you're with me in the work to lower costs, please add your name next to mine to demand Congress works to make life affordable for working families.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125339509/601466210/-1201179575?ms=em26_260213_econ_adv_gq_act___wb_ettx&refcode=em26_260213_econ_adv_gq_act___wb_ettx&source=em26_260213_econ_adv_gq_act___wb_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260213_econ_adv_gq_act___wb_ettx&utm_medium=email&contactdata=kGbDBoYlOgoZPWC536aaCF8I4yN5nowVb8i9u/HIKaFbth+zjAIPhQ3tUw+iMjcmJ5tsme9WsGr4EQufRyCMQ1A2FFct8GzY1oiC/Je/jyZxWkTHWH357ZekTes6whVJ1/AIxJWf57HyyJNyi36hEDcYrYwp98JHzCwZC2RiN4E=&refcode2=ac3e90ce-1a09-f111-832e-0022482a9733&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWMzZTkwY2UtMWEwOS1mMTExLTgzMmUtMDAyMjQ4MmE5NzMzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=dea6B8dRHsiGUKJt5LUhwu0mbzvDpSjgDxNe-SLgckE=&emci=2162c510-0e09-f111-832e-0022482a9733&emdi=ac3e90ce-1a09-f111-832e-0022482a9733&ceid=1020964)**

name: Kat Abughazaleh
subject: We are sick of half measures and partial truths
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Justice Democrats
body:
People want leaders who are willing to put everything on the line for us, not ones who will cave.
#
[](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260213-ka.HEUk4Q&refcode=em20260213-37462&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=37462%2E1203867%2EGXN0jm)
Hi Peter, this is Kat Abughazaleh, a former journalist and Democratic candidate for Congress in Illinois’ 9th district.
**[In a moment, I’m going to ask if you can chip in $5 to support my campaign and Justice Democrats ahead of the March 17th primary election.](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260213-ka.HEUk4Q&refcode=em20260213-37462&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=3&akid=37462%2E1203867%2EGXN0jm)** But first, let me explain why I’m running, and why this race matters to our movement.
I think that every American is sick of the political status quo, the brutality of Republicans, and the feebleness of Democrats. _We are sick of half measures and partial truths._
It’s why I decided to run for Congress in the first place, and it’s why **I’m so proud that our people-powered campaign has been endorsed by Justice Democrats.**
Now more than ever, we need to hold power accountable, and we need leaders who will be held accountable. It doesn’t matter which side you’re on. In fact, I think the most democratic thing you can do as a democracy and as a party is to hold your own team accountable.
Justice Democrats has been on the frontlines of electing new leadership all across the country to revive a party that has bowed down to corporations and the status quo.
**This endorsement reflects something bigger than one race.** It reflects a growing movement of people who are done with a Democratic Party that has cast them aside in favor of profit, greed, and power. People want something different: leaders who are willing to put _everything_ on the line for us, not ones who will cave.
When Americans are getting executed in the streets, we don’t continue to negotiate over how much more money we’ll give the executioners.
When most of us can’t afford to miss a single paycheck, we don’t go along with Republicans and have our benefits cut.
And when a genocide is committed using American tax dollars, our leaders cannot just throw up their hands and pretend that they’re helpless. **If we can’t stand for human rights now, both here and abroad, we can’t stand for anything.**
And if we aren’t willing to criticize our own party to make it better, then there is no way we will be able to defeat Trump and his fascist movement.
It’s time for us to take our political future into our own hands — if the old guard won't step aside, if the establishment continues to calcify, then we’ll beat them at the polls.
But more importantly, I am excited about the movement we are building, about the future that we can create. One where billionaires actually pay their fair share, where workers make a real living wage, and where every person can get the healthcare they need without going into medical debt.
That’s why we need to elect young, bold progressives in districts like IL-09 this year — so we can build something better than what was there before. **This House seat is key to creating a progressive, working-class majority in Congress, but we need YOU to help us win it — especially with AIPAC spending against us.**
**[With just one month until voters make their voices heard in this crowded primary, will you split a grassroots donation of any amount to my campaign and Justice Democrats to help us fight back against AIPAC's spending and win?](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260213-ka.HEUk4Q&refcode=em20260213-37462&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=4&akid=37462%2E1203867%2EGXN0jm)**
**[Contribute $5](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260213-ka.HEUk4Q&refcode=em20260213-37462&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=23&akid=37462%2E1203867%2EGXN0jm)**
I'm honored to be in this fight with you.
In solidarity,
Kat

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/justicedemocrats?refcode=em20260213-37462-footer&t=24&refcode2=37462_1203867_GXN0jm&akid=37462%2E1203867%2EGXN0jm)**

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: They tried to indict me.
body:
---
**They tried to indict me.** On Wednesday, U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro attempted to persuade a Grand Jury to indict me. She failed. I want to walk you through what happened, and then ask for your help in fighting back against this legal intimidation from the Trump administration. The attempt to indict me, and a number of other Members of Congress with service and veteran backgrounds, was in response to a 90-second video that simply quoted the law. Pirro did this at the direction of President Trump, who said repeatedly that I should be investigated, arrested, and hanged for sedition. Thankfully, it was a good day for democracy: A grand jury of anonymous American citizens upheld the rule of law and determined this case should not proceed. But their decision wasn’t just an embarrassing result for the Trump administration, it was another sad day for our country. Because whether or not Pirro succeeded is not the point. The point is that President Trump continues to weaponize our justice system against his perceived enemies. It’s the kind of thing you see in a foreign country, not in the United States we know and love. And if they can do this to me — a sitting United States Senator — what can they do to a business leader or the head of a community foundation or a mom who goes viral on the internet for criticizing Donald Trump? In normal times, this would end this politicized investigation for good, but, of course, I cannot be sure of that. To this point, I have been able to fight back legally because of the support I've received from people like you who have encouraged me, defended me, and donated to help. Today, I am asking for your help once more.
